# QuantDinger Docker Compose - One-Click Deployment
# Usage:
#   1. Copy the unified template and edit your settings
#      cp .env.example .env
#   2. IMPORTANT: Generate and set a secure SECRET_KEY in .env
#      SECRET_KEY=$(python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))")
#      Or edit .env and replace SECRET_KEY value
#   3. docker-compose up -d --build
#   4. Open http://localhost:8888 (web) or http://localhost:8889 (mobile H5)
#
# Backend is built from local source. Frontend and mobile H5 are pulled from
# GHCR. Override tags or image paths via FRONTEND_IMAGE / MOBILE_IMAGE /
# IMAGE_TAG in a project-root `.env`.
# Trading workers use a dedicated 32-connection pool by default. Override it
# with TRADING_DB_POOL_MIN / TRADING_DB_POOL_MAX in the project-root `.env`.
#
# Note: The container will NOT start if SECRET_KEY is using the default value.
#       This is a security measure to prevent insecure deployments.
#
# Docker image sources:
#   Default uses official Docker Hub images.
#   To switch source globally, set a single `IMAGE_PREFIX` in project-root `.env`.
#   Examples: empty (official), `docker.m.daocloud.io/library/`,
#   `docker.xuanyuan.me/library/`.
# Backend Dockerfile uses official Debian/PyPI sources by default.
# For mainland China builds, set BUILD_REGION=cn to use Aliyun mirrors with fallback.
# The backend build defaults to a Docker Hub mirror for python:3.12 because
# Docker Hub auth/base-image pulls are a common first-install failure. Set
# PYTHON_BASE_IMAGE=python:3.12-slim-bookworm to force the official source.

x-backend-build: &backend-build
  context: ./backend_api_python
  dockerfile: Dockerfile
  args:
    BASE_IMAGE: ${PYTHON_BASE_IMAGE:-docker.1ms.run/library/python:3.12-slim-bookworm}
    BUILD_REGION: ${BUILD_REGION:-global}
    APP_VERSION: ${APP_VERSION:-}
    GIT_TAG: ${GIT_TAG:-${IMAGE_TAG:-}}

x-backend-runtime: &backend-runtime
  init: true
  security_opt:
    - no-new-privileges:true
  pids_limit: ${BACKEND_PIDS_LIMIT:-512}
  stop_grace_period: ${BACKEND_STOP_GRACE_PERIOD:-45s}
  logging:
    driver: json-file
    options:
      max-size: ${CONTAINER_LOG_MAX_SIZE:-20m}
      max-file: ${CONTAINER_LOG_MAX_FILES:-5}

x-worker-environment: &worker-environment
  TZ: ${TZ:-Asia/Shanghai}
  LOG_FORMAT: ${LOG_FORMAT:-json}
  DATABASE_URL: postgresql://${POSTGRES_USER:-quantdinger}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-quantdinger123}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-quantdinger}
  DB_TYPE: postgresql
  REDIS_HOST: redis
  REDIS_PORT: 6379
  REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD:-}
  REDIS_CACHE_NAMESPACE: ${REDIS_CACHE_NAMESPACE:-quantdinger:cache:v1}
  CACHE_ENABLED: "true"
  CELERY_TASKS_ENABLED: "true"
  CELERY_REDIS_HOST: redis-jobs
  CELERY_REDIS_PORT: 6379
  CELERY_REDIS_PASSWORD: ${CELERY_REDIS_PASSWORD:-}
  CELERY_BROKER_DB: 0
  CELERY_RESULT_DB: 1
  CELERY_BROKER_URL: ${CELERY_BROKER_URL:-}
  CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND: ${CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND:-}
  DB_POOL_MIN: ${WORKER_DB_POOL_MIN:-2}
  DB_POOL_MAX: ${WORKER_DB_POOL_MAX:-12}
  DB_POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT: ${DB_POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT:-10}
  DB_POOL_HEALTH_CHECK: ${DB_POOL_HEALTH_CHECK:-true}
  DB_APPLICATION_NAME: quantdinger-worker
  SKIP_AUTO_MIGRATE: "true"
  ALLOW_LOCAL_DESKTOP_BROKERS: ${ALLOW_LOCAL_DESKTOP_BROKERS:-true}
  MARKET_CATALOG_AUTO_SYNC: ${MARKET_CATALOG_AUTO_SYNC:-true}
  MARKET_CATALOG_SYNC_INTERVAL_SEC: ${MARKET_CATALOG_SYNC_INTERVAL_SEC:-86400}
  KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS: kafka:9092
  LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_ENTRY: ${LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_ENTRY:-true}
  LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SEC: ${LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SEC:-2.5}
  LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_SEC: ${LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_SEC:-4}
  LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_IDLE_RECONNECT_SEC: ${LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_IDLE_RECONNECT_SEC:-20}
  LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_MAX_CONNECTIONS: ${LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_MAX_CONNECTIONS:-64}

services:
  env-sync:
    build: *backend-build
    image: ${BACKEND_LOCAL_IMAGE:-quantdinger-backend:local}
    container_name: quantdinger-env-sync
    restart: "no"
    entrypoint: ["python", "-m", "app.commands.sync_env", "--workspace", "/workspace"]
    volumes:
      - ./:/workspace
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network

  # ========================
  # PostgreSQL Database
  # ========================
  postgres:
    image: ${POSTGRES_IMAGE:-${IMAGE_PREFIX:-}postgres:18.3-alpine}
    container_name: quantdinger-db
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-quantdinger}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-quantdinger}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-quantdinger123}
      PGDATA: ${POSTGRES_PGDATA:-/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker}
      TZ: ${TZ:-Asia/Shanghai}
    # Raise PostgreSQL's max_connections so API and worker pools plus
    # psql/admin connections remain below PostgreSQL's own limit.
    command:
      - "postgres"
      - "-c"
      - "max_connections=${PG_MAX_CONNECTIONS:-150}"
      - "-c"
      - "shared_buffers=${PG_SHARED_BUFFERS:-256MB}"
    volumes:
      - ${POSTGRES_DATA_SOURCE:-postgres_data}:${POSTGRES_PGDATA:-/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker}
      - ./backend_api_python/migrations/init.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/01-init.sql
    ports:
      - "${DB_PORT:-127.0.0.1:5432}:5432"
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-quantdinger} -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-quantdinger}"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  # ========================
  # Redis (optional cache layer)
  # ========================
  redis:
    image: ${REDIS_IMAGE:-${IMAGE_PREFIX:-}redis:8-alpine}
    container_name: quantdinger-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD:-}
    command:
      - sh
      - -ec
      - |
        if [ -n "$$REDIS_PASSWORD" ]; then set -- --requirepass "$$REDIS_PASSWORD"; fi
        exec redis-server --maxmemory "${REDIS_CACHE_MAXMEMORY:-128mb}" --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru "$$@"
    ports:
      - "${REDIS_BIND:-127.0.0.1:6379}:6379"
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "if [ -n \"$$REDIS_PASSWORD\" ]; then redis-cli --no-auth-warning -a \"$$REDIS_PASSWORD\" ping; else redis-cli ping; fi"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  redis-jobs:
    image: ${REDIS_IMAGE:-${IMAGE_PREFIX:-}redis:8-alpine}
    container_name: quantdinger-redis-jobs
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      REDIS_PASSWORD: ${CELERY_REDIS_PASSWORD:-}
    command:
      - sh
      - -ec
      - |
        if [ -n "$$REDIS_PASSWORD" ]; then set -- --requirepass "$$REDIS_PASSWORD"; fi
        exec redis-server --appendonly yes --appendfsync everysec --save 60 1000 --maxmemory "${REDIS_JOBS_MAXMEMORY:-512mb}" --maxmemory-policy noeviction "$$@"
    volumes:
      - celery_redis_data:/data
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "if [ -n \"$$REDIS_PASSWORD\" ]; then redis-cli --no-auth-warning -a \"$$REDIS_PASSWORD\" ping; else redis-cli ping; fi"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  kafka:
    image: ${KAFKA_IMAGE:-apache/kafka:4.3.1}
    container_name: quantdinger-kafka
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: 1
      KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES: broker,controller
      KAFKA_LISTENERS: CONTROLLER://:9093,PLAINTEXT://:9092,PLAINTEXT_HOST://:29092
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092,PLAINTEXT_HOST://localhost:29092
      KAFKA_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP: CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT_HOST:PLAINTEXT
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES: CONTROLLER
      KAFKA_INTER_BROKER_LISTENER_NAME: PLAINTEXT
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS: 1@kafka:9093
      KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_MIN_ISR: 1
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_NUM_PARTITIONS: ${KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_NUM_PARTITIONS:-12}
      KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_NUM_PARTITIONS: ${KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_NUM_PARTITIONS:-12}
      KAFKA_NUM_PARTITIONS: ${KAFKA_NUM_PARTITIONS:-6}
      KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS: ${KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS:--Xms256m -Xmx768m}
      KAFKA_GROUP_INITIAL_REBALANCE_DELAY_MS: 0
      KAFKA_LOG_DIRS: /var/lib/kafka/data
      CLUSTER_ID: MkU3OEVBNTcwNTJENDM2Qk
    volumes:
      - kafka_data:/var/lib/kafka/data
    ports:
      - "${KAFKA_PORT:-127.0.0.1:29092}:29092"
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "/opt/kafka/bin/kafka-broker-api-versions.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 >/dev/null 2>&1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 20s

  kafka-init:
    <<: *backend-runtime
    build: *backend-build
    image: ${BACKEND_LOCAL_IMAGE:-quantdinger-backend:local}
    container_name: quantdinger-kafka-init
    restart: "no"
    command: ["python", "-m", "app.commands.kafka_topics"]
    depends_on:
      env-sync:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      kafka:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
      - ./.env:/app/.env
    environment:
      KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS: kafka:9092
      KAFKA_REPLICATION_FACTOR: ${KAFKA_REPLICATION_FACTOR:-1}
      KAFKA_MARKET_PARTITIONS: ${KAFKA_MARKET_PARTITIONS:-6}
      KAFKA_STRATEGY_PARTITIONS: ${KAFKA_STRATEGY_PARTITIONS:-12}
      KAFKA_ORDER_PARTITIONS: ${KAFKA_ORDER_PARTITIONS:-12}
      KAFKA_DLQ_PARTITIONS: ${KAFKA_DLQ_PARTITIONS:-3}
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network

  migration:
    <<: *backend-runtime
    build: *backend-build
    image: ${BACKEND_LOCAL_IMAGE:-quantdinger-backend:local}
    container_name: quantdinger-migration
    restart: "no"
    command: ["python", "-m", "app.commands.migrate"]
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
      - backend_logs:/app/logs
      - backend_data:/app/data
      - ./.env:/app/.env
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://${POSTGRES_USER:-quantdinger}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-quantdinger123}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-quantdinger}
      DB_TYPE: postgresql
      DB_POOL_MIN: 1
      DB_POOL_MAX: 2
      DB_APPLICATION_NAME: quantdinger-migration
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network

  # ========================
  # Backend API (Python/Flask)
  # ========================
  backend:
    <<: *backend-runtime
    build: *backend-build
    image: ${BACKEND_LOCAL_IMAGE:-quantdinger-backend:local}
    container_name: quantdinger-backend
    restart: unless-stopped
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 65535
        hard: 65535
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis-jobs:
        condition: service_healthy
      migration:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    ports:
      - "${BACKEND_PORT:-127.0.0.1:5000}:5000"
    volumes:
      - backend_logs:/app/logs
      - backend_data:/app/data
      # Mount .env for runtime config and admin-panel updates
      - ./.env:/app/.env
    environment:
      - PYTHON_API_HOST=0.0.0.0
      - PYTHON_API_PORT=5000
      - INDICATOR_PREVIEW_DIR=${INDICATOR_PREVIEW_DIR:-/app/data/indicator_previews}
      - GIT_TAG=${GIT_TAG:-${IMAGE_TAG:-}}
      - TZ=${TZ:-Asia/Shanghai}
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://${POSTGRES_USER:-quantdinger}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-quantdinger123}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-quantdinger}
      - DB_TYPE=postgresql
      - REDIS_HOST=redis
      - REDIS_PORT=6379
      - REDIS_PASSWORD=${REDIS_PASSWORD:-}
      - REDIS_CACHE_NAMESPACE=${REDIS_CACHE_NAMESPACE:-quantdinger:cache:v1}
      - CACHE_ENABLED=true
      - QD_PROCESS_ROLE=api
      - LOG_FORMAT=${LOG_FORMAT:-json}
      - PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR=/tmp/quantdinger-prometheus
      - STRATEGY_COMMANDS_ENABLED=true
      - CELERY_TASKS_ENABLED=true
      - CELERY_REDIS_HOST=redis-jobs
      - CELERY_REDIS_PORT=6379
      - CELERY_REDIS_PASSWORD=${CELERY_REDIS_PASSWORD:-}
      - CELERY_BROKER_DB=0
      - CELERY_RESULT_DB=1
      - CELERY_BROKER_URL=${CELERY_BROKER_URL:-}
      - CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND=${CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND:-}
      - SKIP_AUTO_MIGRATE=true
      # Database connection pool tuning (see app/utils/db_postgres.py).
      # Defaults are safe for ~50 concurrent DB users; raise if you run many
      # bots or see `connection pool exhausted` errors.
      - DB_POOL_MIN=${DB_POOL_MIN:-2}
      - DB_POOL_MAX=${DB_POOL_MAX:-12}
      - DB_POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT=${DB_POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT:-10}
      - DB_POOL_HEALTH_CHECK=${DB_POOL_HEALTH_CHECK:-true}
      - DB_APPLICATION_NAME=quantdinger-api
      # Route-level executor tuning (each worker may use one DB connection).
      - MARKET_EXECUTOR_WORKERS=${MARKET_EXECUTOR_WORKERS:-6}
      - MARKET_CATALOG_AUTO_SYNC=${MARKET_CATALOG_AUTO_SYNC:-true}
      - PORTFOLIO_EXECUTOR_WORKERS=${PORTFOLIO_EXECUTOR_WORKERS:-3}
      - RESOURCE_FD_COOLDOWN_SEC=${RESOURCE_FD_COOLDOWN_SEC:-180}
      - LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_ENTRY=${LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_ENTRY:-true}
      - LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SEC=${LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SEC:-2.5}
      - LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_SEC=${LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_SEC:-4}
      - LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_IDLE_RECONNECT_SEC=${LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_IDLE_RECONNECT_SEC:-20}
      - LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_MAX_CONNECTIONS=${LIVE_TRADING_WS_ORDER_MAX_CONNECTIONS:-64}
      - PORTFOLIO_MONITOR_DUE_BATCH_LIMIT=${PORTFOLIO_MONITOR_DUE_BATCH_LIMIT:-5}
      - GUNICORN_WORKERS=${GUNICORN_WORKERS:-2}
      - GUNICORN_THREADS=${GUNICORN_THREADS:-4}
      # IBKR needs local TWS or IB Gateway; set false on SaaS cloud (see env.example).
      - ALLOW_LOCAL_DESKTOP_BROKERS=${ALLOW_LOCAL_DESKTOP_BROKERS:-true}
      # Takes precedence over mounted .env (run.py load_dotenv override=False).
      # Include :8000 when using Vite dev server alongside this stack.
      - FRONTEND_URL=${FRONTEND_URL:-http://localhost:8888,http://localhost:8889,http://localhost:8000}
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:5000/api/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3

  # Optional network MCP gateway. It is disabled unless the `mcp` profile is
  # selected and requires separate upstream/inbound tokens.
  # Example:
  #   QUANTDINGER_AGENT_TOKEN=qd_agent_xxx \
  #   QUANTDINGER_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  #   docker compose --profile mcp up -d --build mcp
  mcp:
    profiles: ["mcp"]
    build:
      context: ./mcp_server
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    image: ${MCP_LOCAL_IMAGE:-quantdinger-mcp:local}
    container_name: quantdinger-mcp
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      backend:
        condition: service_healthy
    ports:
      - "${MCP_HOST_BIND:-127.0.0.1}:${MCP_PORT:-7800}:7800"
    environment:
      QUANTDINGER_BASE_URL: http://backend:5000
      QUANTDINGER_AGENT_TOKEN: ${QUANTDINGER_AGENT_TOKEN:-}
      QUANTDINGER_MCP_TRANSPORT: streamable-http
      QUANTDINGER_MCP_HOST: 0.0.0.0
      QUANTDINGER_MCP_PORT: 7800
      QUANTDINGER_MCP_PUBLIC_URL: ${QUANTDINGER_MCP_PUBLIC_URL:-http://localhost:7800}
      QUANTDINGER_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN: ${QUANTDINGER_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN:-}
      # The default port mapping is loopback-only; TLS may terminate upstream.
      QUANTDINGER_MCP_ALLOW_HTTP: ${QUANTDINGER_MCP_ALLOW_HTTP:-true}
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network

  trading-worker:
    <<: *backend-runtime
    build: *backend-build
    image: ${BACKEND_LOCAL_IMAGE:-quantdinger-backend:local}
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      replicas: ${TRADING_WORKER_REPLICAS:-1}
    command: ["python", "-m", "app.commands.trading_worker"]
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      migration:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    volumes:
      - backend_logs:/app/logs
      - backend_data:/app/data
      - ./.env:/app/.env
    environment:
      <<: *worker-environment
      QD_PROCESS_ROLE: trading
      STRATEGY_COMMANDS_ENABLED: "false"
      DB_POOL_MIN: ${TRADING_DB_POOL_MIN:-4}
      DB_POOL_MAX: ${TRADING_DB_POOL_MAX:-32}
      DB_APPLICATION_NAME: quantdinger-trading
      KAFKA_CLIENT_ID: quantdinger-trading
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-m", "app.commands.worker_health", "trading"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  kafka-audit-worker:
    <<: *backend-runtime
    build: *backend-build
    image: ${BACKEND_LOCAL_IMAGE:-quantdinger-backend:local}
    container_name: quantdinger-kafka-audit-worker
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["python", "-m", "app.commands.kafka_audit_worker"]
    depends_on:
      env-sync:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      migration:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      kafka-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    volumes:
      - backend_logs:/app/logs
      - ./.env:/app/.env
    environment:
      <<: *worker-environment
      QD_PROCESS_ROLE: kafka-audit
      DB_POOL_MIN: 1
      DB_POOL_MAX: 3
      DB_APPLICATION_NAME: quantdinger-kafka-audit
      KAFKA_AUDIT_GROUP_ID: quantdinger-runtime-audit-v1
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-m", "app.commands.worker_health", "kafka-audit"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  strategy-dispatcher-worker:
    <<: *backend-runtime
    build: *backend-build
    image: ${BACKEND_LOCAL_IMAGE:-quantdinger-backend:local}
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      replicas: ${STRATEGY_DISPATCHER_REPLICAS:-1}
    command: ["python", "-m", "app.commands.strategy_dispatcher_worker"]
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      migration:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      kafka-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    volumes:
      - backend_logs:/app/logs
      - ./.env:/app/.env
    environment:
      <<: *worker-environment
      QD_PROCESS_ROLE: strategy-dispatcher
      DB_POOL_MIN: 1
      DB_POOL_MAX: 4
      DB_APPLICATION_NAME: quantdinger-strategy-dispatcher
      KAFKA_CLIENT_ID: quantdinger-strategy-dispatcher
      KAFKA_STRATEGY_DISPATCH_GROUP_ID: quantdinger-strategy-dispatch-v1
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-m", "app.commands.worker_health", "strategy-dispatcher"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  strategy-evaluator-worker:
    <<: *backend-runtime
    build: *backend-build
    image: ${BACKEND_LOCAL_IMAGE:-quantdinger-backend:local}
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      replicas: ${STRATEGY_EVALUATOR_REPLICAS:-1}
    command: ["python", "-m", "app.commands.strategy_evaluator_worker"]
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      migration:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      kafka-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    volumes:
      - backend_logs:/app/logs
      - ./.env:/app/.env
    environment:
      <<: *worker-environment
      QD_PROCESS_ROLE: strategy-evaluator
      DB_POOL_MIN: 1
      DB_POOL_MAX: 4
      DB_APPLICATION_NAME: quantdinger-strategy-evaluator
      KAFKA_CLIENT_ID: quantdinger-strategy-evaluator
      KAFKA_STRATEGY_EVALUATOR_GROUP_ID: ${KAFKA_STRATEGY_EVALUATOR_GROUP_ID:-quantdinger-strategy-evaluator-active-v1}
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-m", "app.commands.worker_health", "strategy-evaluator"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  scheduler-worker:
    <<: *backend-runtime
    build: *backend-build
    image: ${BACKEND_LOCAL_IMAGE:-quantdinger-backend:local}
    container_name: quantdinger-scheduler-worker
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["python", "-m", "app.commands.scheduler"]
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      migration:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    volumes:
      - backend_logs:/app/logs
      - backend_data:/app/data
      - ./.env:/app/.env
    environment:
      <<: *worker-environment
      QD_PROCESS_ROLE: scheduler
      DB_APPLICATION_NAME: quantdinger-scheduler
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-m", "app.commands.worker_health", "scheduler"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  celery-worker:
    <<: *backend-runtime
    build: *backend-build
    image: ${BACKEND_LOCAL_IMAGE:-quantdinger-backend:local}
    container_name: quantdinger-celery-worker
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["celery", "-A", "app.celery_app:celery_app", "worker", "--loglevel=INFO", "-Q", "jobs,ai,maintenance", "--concurrency=${CELERY_CONCURRENCY:-2}"]
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis-jobs:
        condition: service_healthy
      migration:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    volumes:
      - backend_logs:/app/logs
      - backend_data:/app/data
      - ./.env:/app/.env
    environment:
      <<: *worker-environment
      QD_PROCESS_ROLE: celery
      DB_APPLICATION_NAME: quantdinger-celery-worker
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-m", "app.commands.worker_health", "celery"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 45s

  celery-beat:
    <<: *backend-runtime
    build: *backend-build
    image: ${BACKEND_LOCAL_IMAGE:-quantdinger-backend:local}
    container_name: quantdinger-celery-beat
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["celery", "-A", "app.celery_app:celery_app", "beat", "--loglevel=INFO", "--schedule=/app/data/celerybeat-schedule"]
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis-jobs:
        condition: service_healthy
      migration:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    volumes:
      - backend_logs:/app/logs
      - backend_data:/app/data
      - ./.env:/app/.env
    environment:
      <<: *worker-environment
      QD_PROCESS_ROLE: celery
      DB_APPLICATION_NAME: quantdinger-celery-beat
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "kill -0 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3

  # ========================
  # Frontend (Nginx serving prebuilt SPA)
  # ========================
  # Default behaviour: pull the prebuilt multi-arch image from GHCR.
  # Local iteration: clone QuantDinger-Vue into `./QuantDinger-Vue/`
  # (gitignored) and layer the build override on top:
  #   docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.build.yml up --build
  # The `build:` block lives in docker-compose.build.yml so users who only
  # pull never need the `./QuantDinger-Vue/` directory to exist (Compose
  # validates build context paths eagerly when `build:` is present).
  frontend:
    # Tag resolution (highest precedence wins):
    #   FRONTEND_TAG   — per-side override, decouples FE from BE
    #   IMAGE_TAG      — unified knob, sets both FE and BE (BE only relevant in ghcr.yml)
    #   latest         — fallback; pin semver in project-root .env (e.g. IMAGE_TAG=5.0.1)
    image: ${FRONTEND_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/openbyteinc/quantdinger-frontend}:${FRONTEND_TAG:-${IMAGE_TAG:-latest}}
    pull_policy: always
    container_name: quantdinger-frontend
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${FRONTEND_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:${FRONTEND_PORT:-8888}:80"
    environment:
      # nginx envsubst will inject this into the proxy_pass directive at start.
      # Override with the backend's reachable URL when deploying outside compose
      # (e.g. Railway: http://${{Backend.RAILWAY_PRIVATE_DOMAIN}}:5000).
      - BACKEND_URL=${BACKEND_URL:-http://backend:5000}
    depends_on:
      - backend
    networks:
      - quantdinger-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3

  # ========================
  # Mobile H5 (Nginx serving prebuilt mobile SPA)
  # ========================
  # Open http://localhost:8889 for the touch-first mobile web client.
  # It proxies /api to the same backend service, so users do not need to
  # manually configure a server URL for the one-click Docker stack.
  mobile:
    image: ${MOBILE_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/openbyteinc/quantdinger-mobile}:${MOBILE_TAG:-${IMAGE_TAG:-latest}}
    pull_policy: always
    container_name: quantdinger-mobile
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${MOBILE_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:${MOBILE_PORT:-8889}:80"
    environment:
      - BACKEND_URL=${BACKEND_URL:-http://backend:5000}

repository.readme:
# niche-finder **YouTube research for creators: find a niche that is growing, see which videos from small channels took off and why, and check your idea before you film it.** [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/pandich93/youtube-niche-finder?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/pandich93/youtube-niche-finder/releases/latest) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/pandich93/youtube-niche-finder/ci.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=CI)](https://github.com/pandich93/youtube-niche-finder/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Coverage](https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json?url=https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2Fpandich93%2Fyoutube-niche-finder%2Fbadges%2Fcoverage.json&query=%24.totals.percent_covered_display&suffix=%25&label=coverage&style=flat-square)](https://github.com/pandich93/youtube-niche-finder/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/github/license/pandich93/youtube-niche-finder?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-100%20tools-8A2BE2?style=flat-square)](backend/README.md#tools) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/pandich93/youtube-niche-finder?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/pandich93/youtube-niche-finder/stargazers) > **Status: the hosted version is coming soon.** Accounts with sign-up, > tariffs and connecting your own channel are built; the online service is > being prepared for its first users. Want early > access? [Open an issue titled "Early access"](https://github.com/pandich93/youtube-niche-finder/issues/new?title=Early%20access) > or star the repository to follow the launch. Can't wait? > [Run your own copy today](docs/self-hosting.md) — it is free and open source. ![niche-finder dashboard: overview — corpus totals, the last 24 hours (new outliers, accelerating videos, growing channels), recent outlier channels and future competition](assets/dashboard.jpg) ## Contents - [What it does for you](#what-it-does-for-you) - [Why niche-finder](#why-niche-finder) - [Screens](#screens) - [Plans](#plans) - [Run it yourself today](#run-it-yourself-today) - [For developers](#for-developers) - [Privacy and security](#privacy-and-security) - [License](#license) ## What it does for you ### Find a niche worth entering - **Where to enter:** every niche scored 0–100 from six visible terms — demand trend, supply growth, newcomers breaking out, RPM, templated channels, policy signals — with a side-by-side comparison of 2–3 niches. - **Viral videos from small channels and outlier channels:** a video against its own channel's median, over any period from 24 hours to 90 days, with subscriber, length, Shorts, RPM and Partner Program filters. - **Niche trend:** growing, stable, cooling or saturated, from the last 30 days against the 90 before — supply, demand, new channels and whether newcomers break out. - **What outliers share:** what a niche's breakouts have in common against ordinary videos — a number or "?" in the title, length, tags, weekday and time — by the numbers. - **Language gaps:** formats that took off in one language and whether anything like them exists in another. - Trending categories and keywords, a niche map, the best time to publish, and export of a niche's videos to CSV. ### Plan your next video - **Idea checker:** is a topic free, recently covered, proven or a flop in this niche? - **Outlier to brief:** one click turns a video that beat its channel into a working brief — hook, title patterns, whether the topic is covered, title candidates and thumbnail references. - **Metadata review and hook score:** your draft title, description, tags and first 30 seconds checked against what worked in the niche. - **Content gaps:** questions from a niche's comments that no video answers yet, ranked by demand. - **Content calendar:** drafts on a week or month grid with the niche's best hours and a reminder the day before. ### Watch competitors and your own channel - **Channel tracking:** growth by window, views per hour of every upload, a revenue range, Partner Program thresholds and the next milestones. - **Alerts:** a new outlier, accelerating views, a title or thumbnail swap, a channel breaking its silence, a new video on a topic you named — on the dashboard, in the browser extension, in Telegram or as a morning digest. - **Repackaging and template risk:** title and thumbnail swaps with views before and after; how much a channel's uploads look like one template repeated. - **Collaboration partners and sponsors:** similar channels of your size, and which brands pay creators in a niche. - **Your own channels:** connect them read-only through Google and see your real views, retention, revenue and RPM next to the niche; a net profit calculator with your own costs. ### Wherever you work - **A web dashboard** with 27 sections plus niche, channel and brief pages. - **A Chrome extension** that puts the numbers on top of YouTube itself. - **Claude Desktop or any MCP client:** 100 tools and 7 ready-made scenarios, so you can ask for a niche in plain words. ## Why niche-finder - **History the API doesn't give you.** YouTube only ever says "how many views right now". niche-finder writes the numbers down on a schedule, so views per hour, acceleration, subscriber growth and title swaps exist. - **Honest numbers.** RPM and revenue come as a range, never one invented figure; every estimate is labelled as niche-finder's, not YouTube's; below a minimum sample you get "not enough data" instead of a guess; there is no opaque "SEO score". - **Answers, not dashboards for their own sake.** Every screen ends in a decision: enter this niche or not, film this idea or not, copy this format or not. - **The same numbers everywhere.** The dashboard, the extension and Claude call the same calculations, so they can never disagree. ## Screens

Viral videos — small channels that beat their expectations
Outlier channels — best video's multiplier against the channel's median

Where to enter — every niche scored 0–100, each term visible, sortable
Idea checker — free, recently covered, proven demand or flop

Channel — growth, snapshots, revenue range, similar channels
Keywords — trendScore, lift, momentum

Repackaging — title and thumbnail changes, before / after
Another language — outliers in English and whether Russian has anything like them

Compare — views by age for up to five videos, side by side
Policy signals — YouTube's three inauthentic-content categories, no risk percentage

Alerts — new outliers and accelerating videos on tracked channels
Find a niche — semantic search over the collected videos
Every screen is described in [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md#screens). ## Plans The hosted service will have a free tier and paid tiers. A tier sets how much you can do per day (YouTube lookups, searches, AI features), how many channels you can track and connect, and which features are on — for example your own channel's revenue, the browser extension and MCP, alerts, export. Prices will be announced at launch; until then, early-access users get the free tier. The tariff system is already built: an admin defines tiers on the dashboard, and users switch between free tiers themselves. See [backend/README.md](backend/README.md#tariffs-saas-sub-project-1-nf_multi_user1). ## Run it yourself today niche-finder is open source. With Docker and a free YouTube API key you can run your own copy in a few minutes — the dashboard, the background worker, the extension and the MCP server for Claude Desktop: ```bash git clone https://github.com/pandich93/youtube-niche-finder.git cd youtube-niche-finder cp .env.example .env # put your key into YOUTUBE_API_KEY docker compose build && make up # then open http://localhost:8080 in your browser ``` The full guide — Claude Desktop, the extension, running without Docker, how it works, giving accounts to other people — is in [docs/self-hosting.md](docs/self-hosting.md). ## For developers | Document | What's inside | |---|---| | [docs/self-hosting.md](docs/self-hosting.md) | install and run your own copy | | [docs/hosting.md](docs/hosting.md) | run one copy on your domain for other people: HTTPS, accounts, mail, backups, monitoring | | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) | YouTube quota, the CLI, all 100 MCP tools and 7 scenarios, tariffs, configuration, formulas, code structure | | [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) | every dashboard screen, where its data comes from, what costs quota | | [extension/README.md](extension/README.md) | what the extension shows on each YouTube page | | [docs/http-api.md](docs/http-api.md) | all 155 HTTP routes with parameters, costs and MCP twins (generated from the code) | | [`.env.example`](.env.example) | every setting, commented in place | | [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) · [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) | dev setup and tests; what changed in each release; how we treat each other | | Path | What's inside | |---|---| | [`backend/`](backend/README.md) | MCP server, HTTP API, worker and CLI — all logic and storage (Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL + pgvector) | | [`frontend/`](frontend/README.md) | the dashboard: plain ES modules, no npm, no build step | | [`extension/`](extension/README.md) | Chrome extension (Manifest V3): panels and badges on top of YouTube | | [`docs/`](docs/README.md) | documentation map, self-hosting guide and the HTTP API reference | | [`scripts/`](scripts) | MCP-in-Docker launcher, diagnostics, the API-docs generator, benchmarks | | [`infra/`](infra) | Caddy HTTPS proxy (MCP over HTTP, and the production site), the scheduled Postgres backup | Bug reports, fixes and documentation PRs are welcome. For anything bigger — a new MCP tool, API route or dashboard screen — please open an issue first. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) explains the dev setup and the tests (`make local-test`, no YouTube key needed). ## Privacy and security - **Read-only.** niche-finder never uploads, comments or changes anything on YouTube. Connecting your channel asks Google for read-only access, and revenue is a separate permission you can skip. - **Your channel, your choice.** Disconnecting a channel revokes the access at Google and deletes its data. - **No selling, no ads, no sharing** of your data. - **Secrets stay secret.** Refresh tokens are encrypted; API keys never appear in URLs or logs. [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md) lists exactly what is stored and where traffic goes; [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) covers reporting a problem and what protects each mode. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). niche-finder is not affiliated with YouTube or Google. It uses the YouTube API Services under [YouTube's API Terms of Service](https://developers.google.com/youtube/terms/api-services-terms-of-service).

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

# Read-only token by default; smoke-test asks for write itself to push the
# coverage badge data.
permissions:
  contents: read

# A new push to the same PR cancels the run still going for the old one; runs
# on main always finish (each one may push the badge).
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  # Fast, no database: runs first so a lint error fails the build before the
  # test job spins up Postgres. Same pinned ruff as `make lint`; the config is
  # backend/pyproject.toml, which ruff finds on its own for files under backend/.
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Lint backend with ruff
        run: |
          pip install ruff==0.16.9
          ruff check backend

      # docs/http-api.md is generated from backend/interfaces/http/api.py:
      # a route added or changed without `make api-docs` fails here.
      - name: Check the HTTP API reference is current
        run: python3 scripts/gen_http_api_docs.py --check

      # A relative link in any tracked .md must reach a tracked file (and a
      # heading, for #anchors): .gitignore skips docs/* except listed pages,
      # so a new page can stay local while four documents already link to it.
      - name: Check the links between documents
        run: python3 scripts/check_doc_links.py

      # backend/requirements.txt is `uv pip compile --universal` output for
      # Python 3.10+ on every OS. Recompiling it (uv keeps the pins already
      # there) must change nothing but comments: a lockfile rewritten by hand
      # or by Dependabot's pip updater drops the per-version and per-OS lines,
      # which only Docker's Python 3.12 on Linux would survive.
      - name: Check the backend lockfile is uv-compiled
        run: |
          pip install uv==0.13.5
          make lock-check UV=uv

  # Every dashboard screen in headless Chromium against a seeded backend
  # (frontend/tests/test_smoke.py). No button clicks: POSTs spend quota.
  frontend-smoke:
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
        env:
          POSTGRES_DB: niches
          POSTGRES_USER: niches
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: niches
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U niches -d niches"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: "pip"
          cache-dependency-path: |
            backend/requirements.txt
            frontend/tests/requirements.txt

      - name: Install backend and smoke-test dependencies
        run: pip install -r backend/requirements.txt -r frontend/tests/requirements.txt

      - uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright
          key: playwright-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('frontend/tests/requirements.txt') }}

      - name: Install Chromium
        run: python -m playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Smoke-test every dashboard screen
        working-directory: backend
        run: python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider ../frontend/tests

      - name: Upload screenshots
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: dashboard-screenshots
          path: frontend/tests/screenshots/

  smoke-test:
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    services:
      postgres:
        image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
        env:
          POSTGRES_DB: niches
          POSTGRES_USER: niches
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: niches
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U niches -d niches"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: "pip"
          cache-dependency-path: backend/requirements.txt

      - name: Install backend dependencies
        run: pip install -r backend/requirements.txt coverage pytest

      # One pytest process for the whole suite: tests/conftest.py gives every
      # file the world it would see running alone -- Postgres-backed files get
      # a fresh schema each (tests/schema_scope.py), and the sqlite-double
      # files keep their doubles in a private module world instead of
      # sys.modules (tests/module_doubles.py). pytest picks up any new
      # test_*.py by itself. The coverage report is printed either way; a test
      # failure fails the step (and skips the badge data) after it.
      - name: Run tests with coverage
        working-directory: backend
        env:
          # The service image ships pgvector: its tests must run, never skip.
          NICHE_REQUIRE_PGVECTOR: "1"
        run: |
          status=0
          coverage run --source=. --omit="tests/*" -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/ || status=$?
          coverage report -m
          if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::pytest exited with status $status"
            exit "$status"
          fi
          coverage json -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/coverage_full.json"
          python3 -c "
          import json, os
          tmp = os.environ['RUNNER_TEMP']
          d = json.load(open(os.path.join(tmp, 'coverage_full.json')))
          json.dump({'totals': d['totals']}, open(os.path.join(tmp, 'coverage.json'), 'w'), indent=2)
          "

      # The badge data lives on its own orphan branch, `badges`, holding just
      # coverage.json -- never on main, so a push to main never races a bot
      # commit. The README badges read it from raw.githubusercontent.com. The
      # branch is created on the first run; a run whose numbers did not change
      # commits nothing; a push that loses a race with a concurrent run is
      # retried on top of the new tip (never forced).
      - name: Publish coverage badge data to the badges branch
        if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          BADGE_SOURCE: ${{ runner.temp }}/coverage.json
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          branch=badges
          remote="${BADGE_REMOTE:-https://x-access-token:${GITHUB_TOKEN}@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git}"
          work="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
          git init -q "$work"
          git -C "$work" config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git -C "$work" config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git -C "$work" remote add origin "$remote"
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            # Runs for close pushes can finish out of order; a run whose
            # commit is no longer main's tip leaves the badge to the newer one.
            main_tip="$(git -C "$work" ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)"
            if [ -n "$main_tip" ] && [ "$main_tip" != "$GITHUB_SHA" ]; then
              echo "main moved on to $main_tip; skipping stale coverage from $GITHUB_SHA."
              exit 0
            fi
            rc=0
            git -C "$work" ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin "$branch" >/dev/null || rc=$?
            if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
              git -C "$work" fetch -q --depth=1 origin "refs/heads/$branch"
              git -C "$work" checkout -q -f -B "$branch" FETCH_HEAD
            elif [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then
              echo "Branch $branch does not exist yet; creating it as an orphan."
              git -C "$work" symbolic-ref HEAD "refs/heads/$branch"
              git -C "$work" update-ref -d "refs/heads/$branch"
              git -C "$work" read-tree --empty
            else
              echo "::error::git ls-remote failed with status $rc"
              exit "$rc"
            fi
            cp "$BADGE_SOURCE" "$work/coverage.json"
            git -C "$work" add coverage.json
            if git -C "$work" diff --cached --quiet; then
              echo "Coverage badge data unchanged; nothing to commit."
              exit 0
            fi
            git -C "$work" commit -q -m "Update coverage badge data [skip ci]"
            if git -C "$work" push -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$branch"; then
              echo "Published coverage badge data to $branch."
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "Push to $branch rejected (attempt $attempt); retrying on the new tip."
          done
          echo "::error::could not push coverage badge data to $branch"
          exit 1

  docker-build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Build web/worker images
        run: docker compose build

      # docs/hosting.md: the production layer must still merge with the base
      # file, Caddy must accept its config, and the backup script must parse.
      - name: Check the production setup
        env:
          NF_DOMAIN: niches.example.com
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ci-only
        run: |
          docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml config -q
          docker run --rm -e NF_DOMAIN \
            -v "$PWD/infra/caddy/Caddyfile.prod:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro" \
            caddy:2-alpine caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile
          sh -n infra/backup/backup.sh

Policy signals — YouTube's three inauthentic-content categories, no risk percentage

Alerts — new outliers and accelerating videos on tracked channels
Find a niche — semantic search over the collected videos
Every screen is described in [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md#screens). ## Plans The hosted service will have a free tier and paid tiers. A tier sets how much you can do per day (YouTube lookups, searches, AI features), how many channels you can track and connect, and which features are on — for example your own channel's revenue, the browser extension and MCP, alerts, export. Prices will be announced at launch; until then, early-access users get the free tier. The tariff system is already built: an admin defines tiers on the dashboard, and users switch between free tiers themselves. See [backend/README.md](backend/README.md#tariffs-saas-sub-project-1-nf_multi_user1). ## Run it yourself today niche-finder is open source. With Docker and a free YouTube API key you can run your own copy in a few minutes — the dashboard, the background worker, the extension and the MCP server for Claude Desktop: ```bash git clone https://github.com/pandich93/youtube-niche-finder.git cd youtube-niche-finder cp .env.example .env # put your key into YOUTUBE_API_KEY docker compose build && make up # then open http://localhost:8080 in your browser ``` The full guide — Claude Desktop, the extension, running without Docker, how it works, giving accounts to other people — is in [docs/self-hosting.md](docs/self-hosting.md). ## For developers | Document | What's inside | |---|---| | [docs/self-hosting.md](docs/self-hosting.md) | install and run your own copy | | [docs/hosting.md](docs/hosting.md) | run one copy on your domain for other people: HTTPS, accounts, mail, backups, monitoring | | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) | YouTube quota, the CLI, all 100 MCP tools and 7 scenarios, tariffs, configuration, formulas, code structure | | [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) | every dashboard screen, where its data comes from, what costs quota | | [extension/README.md](extension/README.md) | what the extension shows on each YouTube page | | [docs/http-api.md](docs/http-api.md) | all 155 HTTP routes with parameters, costs and MCP twins (generated from the code) | | [`.env.example`](.env.example) | every setting, commented in place | | [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) · [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) | dev setup and tests; what changed in each release; how we treat each other | | Path | What's inside | |---|---| | [`backend/`](backend/README.md) | MCP server, HTTP API, worker and CLI — all logic and storage (Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL + pgvector) | | [`frontend/`](frontend/README.md) | the dashboard: plain ES modules, no npm, no build step | | [`extension/`](extension/README.md) | Chrome extension (Manifest V3): panels and badges on top of YouTube | | [`docs/`](docs/README.md) | documentation map, self-hosting guide and the HTTP API reference | | [`scripts/`](scripts) | MCP-in-Docker launcher, diagnostics, the API-docs generator, benchmarks | | [`infra/`](infra) | Caddy HTTPS proxy (MCP over HTTP, and the production site), the scheduled Postgres backup | Bug reports, fixes and documentation PRs are welcome. For anything bigger — a new MCP tool, API route or dashboard screen — please open an issue first. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) explains the dev setup and the tests (`make local-test`, no YouTube key needed). ## Privacy and security - **Read-only.** niche-finder never uploads, comments or changes anything on YouTube. Connecting your channel asks Google for read-only access, and revenue is a separate permission you can skip. - **Your channel, your choice.** Disconnecting a channel revokes the access at Google and deletes its data. - **No selling, no ads, no sharing** of your data. - **Secrets stay secret.** Refresh tokens are encrypted; API keys never appear in URLs or logs. [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md) lists exactly what is stored and where traffic goes; [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) covers reporting a problem and what protects each mode. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). niche-finder is not affiliated with YouTube or Google. It uses the YouTube API Services under [YouTube's API Terms of Service](https://developers.google.com/youtube/terms/api-services-terms-of-service).

# niche-finder -- docker compose
#
#   cp .env.example .env      # then put your YOUTUBE_API_KEY in it
#
# .env is loaded twice: compose reads it for the ${VAR} substitutions below,
# and worker/web/mcp/mcp-http also get it whole via env_file, so any setting
# documented in .env.example (LLM, Ollama, notifications, worker intervals)
# reaches the app without being listed here.
#
# The API key is only needed at runtime, not to build: `docker compose build`
# works with an empty .env. The worker exits with a clear message if the key is
# missing, and the MCP tools that spend quota say so when you call them.
#   docker compose up -d postgres web worker   # база + дашборд на http://localhost:8080 + сборщик
#   docker compose logs -f worker
#   docker compose run --rm mcp        # MCP server on stdio, for manual testing
#   docker compose --profile http up -d mcp-http mcp-https   # MCP over HTTPS on :8765 (/mcp)
#
# The worker and the MCP server share the same Postgres database, so whatever
# the worker collects is immediately visible to the tools.
#
# Claude Desktop launches its own MCP container OUTSIDE this compose project
# (see scripts/mcp-docker.sh) -- that container only reaches Postgres because
# the script joins it to this project's network by name (`niche-finder_default`,
# derived from `name: niche-finder` below). That network only exists once
# `docker compose up` has been run at least once.

name: niche-finder

x-common: &common
  build:
    context: ./backend
    args:
      PREFETCH_MODEL: "${PREFETCH_MODEL:-0}"
  image: niche-finder:latest
  # Every service built from this block gets the whole .env (LLM_*, OLLAMA_*,
  # NOTIFY_*, WORKER_*...). Keys under `environment` win over env_file.
  env_file:
    - path: .env
      required: false
  environment:
    YOUTUBE_API_KEY: "${YOUTUBE_API_KEY:-}"
    POSTGRES_HOST: "${POSTGRES_HOST:-postgres}"
    POSTGRES_PORT: "${POSTGRES_PORT:-5432}"
    POSTGRES_DB: "${POSTGRES_DB:-niches}"
    POSTGRES_USER: "${POSTGRES_USER:-niches}"
    POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-niches}"
    # .env may point this at localhost:5433 for running outside Docker; it beats
    # POSTGRES_* in _dsn(), so blank it inside containers. Repeated in every
    # service that overrides `environment` (YAML merge doesn't deep-merge).
    NICHE_DATABASE_URL: ""
    TZ: "${TZ:-Asia/Tashkent}"
  volumes:
    - models:/models
  restart: unless-stopped
  depends_on:
    postgres:
      condition: service_healthy

services:
  # Persistence. Everything worker/web/mcp/mcp-http read and write lives here
  # now instead of in a SQLite file on the `data` volume.
  postgres:
    # stage 06: pgvector/pgvector:pg16 is upstream postgres:16 (debian, not
    # alpine) plus the pgvector extension pre-installed -- same major
    # version, same data directory format, so the existing postgres-data
    # volume survives the swap. schema.py detects the extension at every
    # init_db() and only uses it when present, so nothing breaks on an
    # older/plain postgres:16 image either. See README's "pgvector rollback"
    # section before running `docker compose up -d postgres` on a database
    # that matters -- back up the volume first, this is a one-way image swap.
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
    container_name: niche-finder-postgres
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: "${POSTGRES_DB:-niches}"
      POSTGRES_USER: "${POSTGRES_USER:-niches}"
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-niches}"
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    # Published to 127.0.0.1 only (same philosophy as `web` below) so
    # `python3 server.py` outside Docker, psql, or a GUI client can reach it,
    # without exposing the database to the local network.
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${POSTGRES_HOST_PORT:-5433}:5432"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-niches} -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-niches}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10

  # Keeps the corpus fresh and writes the stats history that velocity,
  # acceleration and period-over-period comparisons are computed from.
  worker:
    <<: *common
    container_name: niche-finder-worker
    command: ["python", "worker.py"]
    # Код монтируется из папки, а не берётся из образа: образ нужен только
    # ради Python и зависимостей, поэтому правка в backend/ применяется
    # обычным `docker compose restart worker`, без пересборки.
    volumes:
      - models:/models
      - ./backend:/app:ro
    environment:
      YOUTUBE_API_KEY: "${YOUTUBE_API_KEY:-}"
      POSTGRES_HOST: "${POSTGRES_HOST:-postgres}"
      POSTGRES_PORT: "${POSTGRES_PORT:-5432}"
      POSTGRES_DB: "${POSTGRES_DB:-niches}"
      POSTGRES_USER: "${POSTGRES_USER:-niches}"
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-niches}"
      NICHE_DATABASE_URL: ""
      TZ: "${TZ:-Asia/Tashkent}"
      # how often to re-read counters for videos published in the last WORKER_HOT_PERIOD
      WORKER_HOT_INTERVAL_MIN: "${WORKER_HOT_INTERVAL_MIN:-180}"
      WORKER_HOT_PERIOD: "${WORKER_HOT_PERIOD:-7d}"
      WORKER_HOT_LIMIT: "${WORKER_HOT_LIMIT:-1000}"
      # backfill embeddings for videos collected without one; WORKER_EMBED=0 turns it off
      WORKER_EMBED_INTERVAL_MIN: "${WORKER_EMBED_INTERVAL_MIN:-60}"
      WORKER_EMBED_BATCH: "${WORKER_EMBED_BATCH:-500}"
      WORKER_EMBED: "${WORKER_EMBED:-1}"
      WORKER_DAILY_INTERVAL_MIN: "${WORKER_DAILY_INTERVAL_MIN:-1440}"
      WORKER_FULL_PERIOD: "${WORKER_FULL_PERIOD:-30d}"
      WORKER_FULL_LIMIT: "${WORKER_FULL_LIMIT:-3000}"
      WORKER_REGIONS: "${WORKER_REGIONS:-US}"
      WORKER_TRENDING: "${WORKER_TRENDING:-1}"
      # comma-separated topics kept continuously fresh (1 search call each per day)
      WORKER_QUERIES: "${WORKER_QUERIES:-}"
      WORKER_QUERY_PERIOD: "${WORKER_QUERY_PERIOD:-24h}"
      WORKER_QUERY_PAGES: "${WORKER_QUERY_PAGES:-1}"

  # Дашборд: FastAPI отдаёт /api/* и статику из ./frontend.
  # Слушает только 127.0.0.1 -- внутри контейнера лежит ваш ключ YouTube,
  # выставлять его в локальную сеть незачем.
  web:
    <<: *common
    container_name: niche-finder-web
    # Самолечение: если образ собран без fastapi/uvicorn (например, Docker Hub
    # был недоступен и пересобрать не вышло), ставим их при старте с pypi —
    # это другой хост, он обычно доступен, даже когда registry отвалился.
    # На нормально собранном образе проверка занимает миллисекунды.
    command:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        python -c 'import fastapi, uvicorn' 2>/dev/null || {
          echo 'fastapi/uvicorn нет в образе — ставлю с pypi (разово, ~30 сек)';
          pip install --quiet --user --no-warn-script-location \
            'fastapi>=0.115' 'uvicorn[standard]>=0.30' || {
              echo 'Не удалось поставить зависимости. Нужен доступ к pypi.org'; exit 1; };
        }
        exec python -m uvicorn api:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080
    environment:
      YOUTUBE_API_KEY: "${YOUTUBE_API_KEY:-}"
      POSTGRES_HOST: "${POSTGRES_HOST:-postgres}"
      POSTGRES_PORT: "${POSTGRES_PORT:-5432}"
      POSTGRES_DB: "${POSTGRES_DB:-niches}"
      POSTGRES_USER: "${POSTGRES_USER:-niches}"
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-niches}"
      NICHE_DATABASE_URL: ""
      FRONTEND_DIR: /frontend
      TZ: "${TZ:-Asia/Tashkent}"
    volumes:
      - models:/models
      - ./backend:/app:ro
      - ./frontend:/frontend:ro
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${WEB_PORT:-8080}:8080"

  # MCP over stdio. Not started by `up` -- Claude Desktop launches its own
  # container via scripts/mcp-docker.sh, joined to this project's network by
  # name so it can still reach `postgres`. Use `docker compose run --rm mcp`
  # to poke at it by hand from inside the compose project itself.
  mcp:
    <<: *common
    profiles: ["manual"]
    stdin_open: true
    tty: false
    restart: "no"
    command: ["python", "server.py"]
    # Как и остальные сервисы, запускает код прямо из ./backend — образ нужен
    # только ради Python и зависимостей. Пересборка требуется лишь тогда,
    # когда меняется requirements.txt.
    volumes:
      - models:/models
      - ./backend:/app:ro

  # MCP over streamable HTTP, for clients that prefer a URL to a subprocess.
  mcp-http:
    <<: *common
    container_name: niche-finder-mcp-http
    profiles: ["http"]
    command: ["python", "server.py"]
    environment:
      YOUTUBE_API_KEY: "${YOUTUBE_API_KEY:-}"
      POSTGRES_HOST: "${POSTGRES_HOST:-postgres}"
      POSTGRES_PORT: "${POSTGRES_PORT:-5432}"
      POSTGRES_DB: "${POSTGRES_DB:-niches}"
      POSTGRES_USER: "${POSTGRES_USER:-niches}"
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-niches}"
      NICHE_DATABASE_URL: ""
      MCP_TRANSPORT: streamable-http
      MCP_HOST: 0.0.0.0
      # Without NF_MULTI_USER=1 there is no sign-in, and server.py refuses a
      # non-loopback address unless told it is intended (plan P1-15). Here it
      # is: this port is not published, only the compose network and
      # mcp-https (127.0.0.1 only) reach it. docker-compose.prod.yml turns it off.
      MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED: "1"
      MCP_PORT: "8765"
    # No host port here on purpose -- only mcp-https (below) is published to
    # the host. Plain HTTP stays inside the niche-finder_default network,
    # reachable by other containers as mcp-http:8765.

  # TLS front door for mcp-http: terminates HTTPS with a locally-trusted
  # certificate (Caddy's internal CA) so a same-machine client -- e.g. Claude
  # Desktop configured with {"url": "https://localhost:8765/mcp", "type": "http"} --
  # gets a real HTTPS URL without a public domain or tunnel.
  mcp-https:
    image: caddy:2-alpine
    container_name: niche-finder-mcp-https
    profiles: ["http"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - mcp-http
    volumes:
      - ./infra/caddy/Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - caddy-data:/data
      - caddy-config:/config
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${MCP_PORT:-8765}:8765"

  # Stage 11: fully local LLM enrichment -- nothing leaves the machine.
  # Opt-in (`docker compose --profile llm-local up -d ollama`) because it
  # pulls a multi-GB image and model on first run. Point LLM_PROVIDER=ollama
  # and OLLAMA_URL=http://ollama:11434 at it from `.env` once it's up; web/
  # worker/mcp reach it by service name on the same compose network. Running
  # `ollama serve` on the host instead (not in Docker) works too -- that's
  # what DEFAULT_OLLAMA_URL in factory.py assumes when this service isn't used.
  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama:latest
    container_name: niche-finder-ollama
    profiles: ["llm-local"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ollama-data:/root/.ollama
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${OLLAMA_HOST_PORT:-11434}:11434"

volumes:
  postgres-data:
    name: niche-finder-postgres-data
  models:
    name: niche-finder-models
  caddy-data:
    name: niche-finder-caddy-data
  caddy-config:
    name: niche-finder-caddy-config
  ollama-data:
    name: niche-finder-ollama-data

repository.readme:
The Open-Source Workplace AI Platform

Website · Docs · Discord · Roadmap




**Translations:** [Français](docs/i18n/fr/README.md) · [Deutsch](docs/i18n/de/README.md) · [简体中文](docs/i18n/zh-CN/README.md) · [日本語](docs/i18n/ja/README.md) · [Русский](docs/i18n/ru/README.md) · [עברית](docs/i18n/he/README.md) · [한국어](docs/i18n/ko/README.md) · [Español](docs/i18n/es/README.md) · [Português](docs/i18n/pt/README.md) · [Türkçe](docs/i18n/tr/README.md) · [Tiếng Việt](docs/i18n/vi/README.md) · [Italiano](docs/i18n/it/README.md) · [Čeština](docs/i18n/cs/README.md)

PipesHub - Explainable & Extensible

[PipesHub](https://www.pipeshub.com/) is an open-source platform for connecting AI applications to the knowledge stored across your company's business systems. Connect Slack, Google Drive, GitHub, Microsoft 365, Notion and 50+ other systems. Search across them and get answers with citations, filtered by what each person is allowed to see — or give that same context to your own agents, workflows and MCP clients. > [!TIP] > Deploy with a single command: > ```bash > curl -fsSL https://get.pipeshub.com/install | bash > ```


▶ Watch the 2½-minute demo: Claude Code answering from Jira, Slack, GitHub and Drive, with each person's permissions

## What can you build with PipesHub? Don't just use PipesHub — build on it. **[Give Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex secure access to your company's knowledge →](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/examples/tree/main/company-knowledge-mcp)** About ten minutes once PipesHub is running with data indexed. Mint a Personal Access Token (no admin needed), connect your assistant (one command for Claude Code, one config file for Cursor or Codex), and ask *"why was the retry logic in the billing worker changed?"* — it answers from the incident postmortem, the pull request, the chat thread, and the design doc, each cited, and only if you're allowed to see them. Want the same retrieval inside your own code, or behind a search box for your team? The [SDK starter and search example](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/examples) cover both. Built something? [Show us](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/examples/issues/new?template=showcase.yml). ## PipesHub in Action ### Connectors ### Citations ### All Records ### Knowledge Search ## Features **Answers you can trust** - 📝 **Explainable Answers:** PipesHub delivers grounded answers with precise block citations to the original documents. - 🔒 **Permission-Aware Search:** Enforces source-level access controls so users only see what they're authorized to. - 🧠 **Bring Your Own Model, Fully Self-Hostable:** Any LLM provider, deployed in your VPC — data never leaves your infrastructure. **Connected to your systems** - 🔌 **Enterprise Connectors:** 50+ connectors with real-time and scheduled indexing out of the box. - 🕸️ **Knowledge Graph Retrieval:** Graph-backed retrieval that captures relationships across enterprise data. - 🎙️ **Multimodal Support:** Image, diagram, and scanned-file understanding plus voice-based interaction. **What you can build** - 🔍 **Unified Search, Deep Research, and Agents:** Search, Q&A, deep research, web search, and AI agents on one context layer. - 🤖 **No-Code Agents and Actions:** Build agents visually and execute actions across enterprise tools. - 📊 **Artifacts and Code Execution:** Generate reports, charts, and dashboards in a safe execution sandbox. - 🛠️ **Developer-First and Extensible:** APIs, SDKs, MCP tools, custom connectors, and independently scalable services. ## PipesHub Cloud Prefer a fully managed PipesHub without running your own infrastructure? Sign up for **[PipesHub Cloud](https://app.pipeshub.com)**: the same connectors, permission-aware search, and APIs, with nothing to install. Coding agents connect to `https://app.pipeshub.com/mcp` with a personal access token. See [For coding agents](https://docs.pipeshub.com/for-agents). ## Connectors

## 🚀 Deployment Guide PipesHub can be run locally or deployed on any server using Docker Compose. The interactive installer handles all configuration — including secrets, graph DB, broker, and image tag selection — and generates a `.env` for you. > **HTTPS on cloud servers:** If you deploy PipesHub on a cloud server, use an HTTPS endpoint. Browsers block certain requests over plain HTTP. Use Cloudflare, Nginx, or Traefik to terminate TLS. A white screen after HTTP-only deployment is typically caused by this restriction. --- ### ⚡ Quickstart (Recommended) Requires [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) with Compose v2. One command: ```bash curl -fsSL https://get.pipeshub.com/install | bash ``` This downloads the deployment files for the latest release into `./pipeshub` and launches the interactive installer. Open **http://localhost:3000** once it finishes. > **Prefer to read before running?** Download and inspect the script first: > > ```bash > curl -fsSL https://get.pipeshub.com/install -o pipeshub-install.sh > less pipeshub-install.sh # review it > bash pipeshub-install.sh > ``` The installer will: - Check Docker, RAM, and disk prerequisites - Ask whether you want a **slim** or **full** deployment - Let you optionally customise the graph DB, message broker, and KV store - Generate randomised secrets and write a `.env` file - Pull images and start the stack - Wait for PipesHub to become healthy, verify it is reachable, and print the URL ### 🛠️ From a cloned repository (developers) To build from source, contribute, or pin the installer to your checkout: ```bash git clone https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai.git cd pipeshub-ai # Same installer, run from the repo root ./install.sh ``` Building local images from source requires this cloned-repo path (`./install.sh --build`); the one-command installer above always uses prebuilt images. #### Installer options | Flag | Description | |------|-------------| | `-y` / `--yes` | Accept all defaults; skip interactive prompts (CI-friendly) | | `--version TAG` | Pin a specific image tag, e.g. `--version 0.7.0` | | `--reconfigure` | Re-run the wizard and overwrite an existing `.env` | | `--print-env-only` | Write `.env` and print the compose command without starting containers | > **Advanced options:** CI environment variables, slim vs. full deployment types, manual Compose profile usage, and local source builds are covered in [Advanced Deployment Options](deployment/docker-compose/ADVANCED_DEPLOYMENT.md). ## Build with PipesHub The built-in search experience is one way to use PipesHub. The same connected, permission-filtered context is available to your own agents and applications — over MCP for any compatible client, or through the SDKs when you are calling it from your own code. An agent connects as a specific person rather than as the application, so it retrieves exactly what that person is allowed to see. Access is resolved when the query runs, against the source system's own permissions, instead of being approximated at build time. Step-by-step tutorials for the most common builds — an MCP for your coding assistant, private enterprise search, and SDK starters — live in [**pipeshub-ai/examples**](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/examples). The reference material for each building block is below. ### MCP Server Use PipesHub with any MCP-compatible client to bring your enterprise context into AI workflows. Check the README for setup and usage. **Repository:** [pipeshub-ai/mcp-server](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/mcp-server/) #### Connecting an Omnigent agent First, mint a long-lived credential: **workspace → Developer settings → Personal Access Tokens → New token**. Pick an expiry (30/90/365 days, or never) — this runs as *you*, so results respect your own per-user permissions, unlike an OAuth app's client-credentials flow. Three ways to connect, from least to most setup: 1. **Attach in the Omnigent web UI (fastest, no clone).** Open a session's info panel → Manage MCP Servers → add PipesHub's URL and an `Authorization: Bearer ` header → restart the session. 2. **Run the packaged example agent.** A ready-made agent bundle (tuned prompt + instructions) ships with Omnigent: `PIPESHUB_MCP_URL=... PIPESHUB_MCP_TOKEN=... omnigent run examples/pipeshub/`. 3. **Use the connect kit** in [`integrations/omnigent/`](integrations/omnigent/) (`setup.sh` / `run.sh`) for CI, service accounts, or password/OAuth client-credentials auth instead of a personal token. ### SDKs PipesHub provides developer SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and Go to help you integrate quickly. Check the respective SDK repository README for setup and usage details. | Name | Description | Link | |------|-------------|------| | **Python SDK** | Python SDK for PipesHub | [pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-sdk-python](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-sdk-python) | | **TypeScript SDK** | TypeScript SDK for PipesHub | [pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-sdk-typescript](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-sdk-typescript) | | **Go SDK** | Go SDK for PipesHub | [pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-sdk-go](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-sdk-go) | > Need an SDK in another language? Reach out to us at developer@pipeshub.com ## RoadMap

We ship in the open. Here's what's done and what's next:

  • ✅ 🤖 Workplace AI agents: first-class no-code agent builder
  • ✅ 🔗 MCP (Model Context Protocol) support, both server and client
  • ✅ 🧰 Developers SDKs
  • ✅ 🔍 Code search across GitHub and GitLab
  • ⬜ 👤 Personalized search based on team, role, and history
  • ✅ ☸️ Production Kubernetes deployment with HA defaults
  • ⬜ 📈 PageRank-augmented relevance across the knowledge graph

👉 View the full product roadmap on Notion

## 👥 Contributing Want to join our community of developers? Please check out our [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more details on how to set up the development environment, our coding standards, and the contribution workflow.

Where to go for what

Ask a question or get helpDiscord
Report a bug or request a featureGitHub Issues
Report a security issueReport Security Issue
Read the docsPipeshub Docs
See what changed in each releaseChangelog
## FAQ ### What is PipesHub? PipesHub is an open-source platform for connecting AI applications to the knowledge stored across your company's business systems. It connects systems such as Slack, Google Drive, GitHub, Microsoft 365 and Notion, then makes what they hold available in two ways: permission-aware search with citations for your team, and trusted context for your AI agents through APIs, SDKs and MCP. Agents get the same governed view of your company's knowledge that a person would, with the same access controls applied, so they can answer from real company data instead of guessing across tools. You can use the built-in search experience, or build your own agents, workflows and applications on top of it. ### How is PipesHub different from other workplace AI tools? PipesHub is fully open-source (Apache 2.0) and self-hostable — your data never leaves your infrastructure. It features permission-aware search that enforces source-level access controls, and delivers explainable answers with precise block citations to original documents. ### What connectors does PipesHub support? PipesHub has 50+ enterprise connectors with real-time and scheduled indexing. See the [connectors overview](https://docs.pipeshub.com/connectors/overview). ### What file formats can PipesHub index? PDF (including scans), Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), Google Docs/Sheets/Slides, Markdown, HTML, CSV, plain text, and images. Audio and video can be stored but are not indexed yet. Storage accepts a wider set of MIME types — see [Supported MIME Types](https://docs.pipeshub.com/system-overview/storage). ### How do I deploy PipesHub? ```bash curl -fsSL https://get.pipeshub.com/install | bash ``` This writes Compose files into `./pipeshub` and starts the interactive installer. Open **http://localhost:3000** when it finishes. Use HTTPS for cloud deployments — HTTP may cause frontend security blocks. Developers building from source should clone the repository and run `./install.sh` (or `./install.sh --build`) from the repo root. See the [Deployment Guide](#-deployment-guide). ### What LLM providers does PipesHub support? PipesHub is "Bring Your Own Model" — you can use any LLM provider. Deploy in your VPC with your preferred models. ### What is the tech stack? PipesHub has three parts: - **Web app** (Next.js) — search, chat, and admin in the browser. - **API** (Node.js) — accounts, permissions, knowledge bases, and files. - **Python services** — connectors sync your sources; indexing parses documents; query answers with citations. Those services call **AI models you bring**. An **embedding model** turns parsed text into vectors for search. An **LLM** writes the cited answer. Use any provider or a local model (Ollama); a local embedding server is the default. Data sits in a knowledge graph (Neo4j by default, or ArangoDB), a vector store (Qdrant), and MongoDB. Redis is the cache. Files live on disk or object storage. Services hand work to each other over Redis on a local machine, or Kafka in a larger deployment. See the [system overview](https://docs.pipeshub.com/system-overview). ### What is the Knowledge Graph Retrieval feature? PipesHub uses graph-backed retrieval that captures relationships across enterprise data. It uses Neo4j or ArangoDB as graph databases, combined with Qdrant for vector similarity search. ### Does PipesHub have an MCP server? Yes. PipesHub provides an MCP server for integration with any MCP-compatible client. Repository: [pipeshub-ai/mcp-server](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/mcp-server/). ### What SDKs are available? PipesHub provides SDKs for: - **Python**: [pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-sdk-python](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-sdk-python) - **TypeScript**: [pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-sdk-typescript](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-sdk-typescript) - **Go**: [pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-sdk-go](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-sdk-go) ### Can I build AI agents without coding? Yes. PipesHub has a no-code agent builder. You can build agents visually and execute actions across enterprise tools without writing code. ### What is the multimodal support? PipesHub supports image, diagram, and scanned-file understanding, plus voice-based interaction. It uses Docling and pdfplumber for document parsing, or a multimodal LLM (VLM) for scanned PDF OCR. ### How do I troubleshoot deployment issues? 1. Ensure HTTPS is configured for cloud deployments 2. Check Docker compose logs: `docker compose logs` 3. Verify environment variables in env.template 4. Consult [docs.pipeshub.com](https://docs.pipeshub.com/) for detailed guides ### Where can I get help? - [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/K5RskzJBm2) — Ask questions and get help - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai/issues) — Report bugs or request features - [PipesHub Docs](https://docs.pipeshub.com/) — Read the documentation

It helps the project reach the teams who need it.

Built with ❤️ by the PipesHub team and contributors around the world.
