[project]
name = "lilbee"
version = "0.6.90b449"
description = "The whole local AI stack in one executable: run and manage local AI models across every GPU you have, and search your files, code, and the web pages you crawl, with answers that cite the source. Per-project libraries, semantic and hybrid search, vision OCR, an auto-built wiki, CLI, TUI, MCP server, REST API, and Python library. No model server, no database server, no containers. Works with your own Ollama or LM Studio models too."
license = "MIT"
authors = [{ name = "tobocop2", email = "5562156+tobocop2@users.noreply.github.com" }]
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dynamic = ["readme"]
keywords = [
    "rag", "local-rag", "local-llm", "local-ai",
    "mcp", "mcp-server", "model-context-protocol",
    "semantic-search", "vector-search", "retrieval",
    "embeddings", "knowledge-base", "knowledge-management",
    "huggingface", "ocr", "web-crawler",
    "model-manager", "llama-cpp", "gguf", "multi-gpu", "ollama", "lm-studio",
    "obsidian", "second-brain", "personal-ai", "self-hosted", "privacy", "cli", "tui",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Environment :: Console",
    "Environment :: Web Environment",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: End Users/Desktop",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
    "Topic :: Text Processing :: Indexing",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]

dependencies = [
    "lancedb>=0.40",
    "xberg>=1.3.2",
    # The engine user-lock protocol leans on release(), is_singleton reentrancy
    # and the SoftFileLock fallback; the ceiling is the line verified against it.
    "filelock>=4.1.1,<4.2",
    "tree-sitter-language-pack>=1.8.0,<2.0",
    "typer>=0.12",
    "tiktoken",
    "textual>=0.75",
    # Floor is 2.2.0: it bounds StreamableHTTP sessions (CVE-2026-59951); 1.x lacks mcp.server.mcpserver.
    "mcp>=2.2.0,<3",
    "pillow>=13.0.0",
    "litestar>=2.0",
    "uvicorn>=0.30",
    "httpx",
    "diskcache>=5.6.1",
    "jinja2>=2.11.3",
    "typing-extensions>=4.5.0",
    "huggingface_hub>=1.27.0",
    "psutil>=5.9",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.14.2",
    # 2.5 drops the 3.11 floor and ships 3.12-only stubs mypy rejects at the 3.11 target.
    "numpy<2.5",
    # Entity schema patterns are LLM-authored, so their matches need a wall-clock
    # bound; regex takes a per-match timeout where the stdlib re module cannot.
    # Already present transitively via tiktoken.
    "regex",
    # llama.cpp's own Python package, for the ggml block and type sizes the
    # download-size estimate prices a quant with. It is not a second GGUF
    # reader: gguf-parser is, built from the pin that builds llama-server.
    # 0.19 is the first release that names NVFP4. Adds no new package to the
    # install: numpy, pyyaml, requests and tqdm all already arrive with
    # huggingface_hub, lancedb and lilbee itself.
    "gguf>=0.19",
    # The read side is stdlib tomllib; this is its write half.
    "tomli-w>=1.0",
    "cachetools>=7.1.4",
    # gitignore-syntax matching for .lilbeeignore. Already present transitively;
    # the floor is where the non-deprecated "gitignore" pattern factory lands.
    "pathspec>=1.1.1",
    # Chat export pairs parsed heading tags with the raw lines and raises on a
    # mismatch, so a parser change can crash the export. Already present
    # transitively through rich and textual; the floor is the version the
    # export was fuzz-tested against, and the ceiling keeps it off the next
    # major.
    "markdown-it-py>=4.2.0,<5",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# The bundled llama-server and gguf-parser. Not a hard dependency because the
# distribution is published on lilbee.sh rather than PyPI, and a hard reference
# to a name PyPI answers 404 for made the documented install command backtrack
# to a months-old release that predated it. Installing without this leaves a
# working lilbee that says what to install the moment it needs an engine.
# The floor is below every published engine wheel (they carry lilbee's own
# version), so it never excludes a real release; its jobs are to keep the
# in-repo 0.0.0 stub from satisfying an index install and, because the
# specifier names a pre-release, to let plain `pip` resolve the beta-versioned
# wheels without `--pre`.
engine = ["lilbee-engine>=0.6.90b1"]
litellm = ["litellm>=1.84.0,<1.99"]
graph = ["spacy>=3.8", "graspologic-native>=1.2"]
# playwright installs the headless Chromium shell that browser-mode crawls launch.
# ada-url parses a page address with the URL standard the crawler keys pages by.
crawler = ["crawlberg>=1.12.0", "playwright>=1.61.0", "ada-url>=4.0.0"]
# A fallback source of the CUDA 12 runtime, from NVIDIA's official PyPI wheels;
# fleet.cuda_runtime adds their lib dirs to the engine's LD_LIBRARY_PATH. The engine
# wheel now ships cudart/cublas/cublasLt beside llama-server on both Linux and Windows
# (build_llama_server.sh), so this is only needed for an engine built elsewhere.
# Linux x86_64 only: macOS and aarch64 have no CUDA build to feed.
cuda12 = [
    "nvidia-cuda-runtime-cu12; platform_system=='Linux' and platform_machine=='x86_64'",
    "nvidia-cublas-cu12; platform_system=='Linux' and platform_machine=='x86_64'",
    "nvidia-cuda-nvrtc-cu12; platform_system=='Linux' and platform_machine=='x86_64'",
]
release = ["lilbee[crawler,litellm,graph]"]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://lilbee.sh/"
Repository = "https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee"
Issues = "https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/issues"

[project.scripts]
lilbee = "lilbee.runtime.launcher:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

# The README shows each demo as a GitHub video player, which only GitHub
# renders. hatch_build.py rewrites those back to the gh-pages GIFs so the PyPI
# page keeps its moving pictures instead of a wall of links.
[tool.hatch.metadata.hooks.custom]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/lilbee"]

# Dev resolves the bundled engine from the in-repo wheel package; CI fills its
# bin/ with the self-contained llama-server + llama-swap + gguf-parser before
# building. Release installs (`pip install lilbee`) resolve `lilbee-engine` from
# the index instead -- this source override is workspace metadata, not published deps.
[tool.uv.sources]
lilbee-engine = { path = "packaging/engine-wheel" }

# `uv pip install <checkout>[engine] --extra-index-url ...` applies the source
# above no matter the specifier (uv drops version bounds on sourced packages),
# so it silently installed the binariless stub where the deployment wanted the
# real engine wheel. This turns sources off for the `uv pip` interface only:
# that command now resolves lilbee-engine from the index, while `uv sync` /
# `uv lock` (the project interface) keep using the stub.
[tool.uv.pip]
no-sources = true

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    # The bundled engine is an optional extra for users, because the wheel is
    # published on lilbee.sh rather than PyPI and a hard reference to a name
    # PyPI answers 404 for breaks the documented install. Development and CI
    # still need it: the pin test reads its metadata, and the local source
    # below makes it a workspace path rather than an index lookup.
    "lilbee-engine",
    # The self-check-extras charset probe and its tests call chardet directly;
    # without this, chardet only arrives via the crawler extra, and the bare
    # `uv sync --locked` CI test env cannot run those tests.
    "chardet>=7",
    # The saved-page names and their tests parse addresses with ada-url, which
    # otherwise only the crawler and release extras install.
    "ada-url>=4.0.0",
    # The crawl tests sign a certificate for a local HTTPS site.
    "cryptography>=44",
    "hypothesis>=6.100",
    "mypy>=1.19.1",
    "packaging>=24",
    "pytest",
    "pytest-asyncio",
    "pytest-cov",
    "reportlab",
    "ruff>=0.15.4",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "pytest-httpserver",
    "types-pyyaml>=6.0.12.20250915",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    "pytest-forked>=1.6.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.3",
    "pre-commit>=4.0",
    "types-cachetools>=7.0.0.20260713",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = [".", "tests"]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
addopts = "--ignore=tests/integration"
timeout = 60
markers = [
    "slow: integration tests that download models or take >10s",
    "real_model_classify: opt out of the global _classify_installed_models mock",
    "real_litellm_probe: opt out of the global litellm_available True override",
    "real_engine_resolution: opt out of the engine-binary seal (host PATH and LILBEE_LLAMA_SERVER_PATH resolve again)",
    "xdist_group: pin grouped tests to a single xdist worker for serial execution",
    "no_health_default: opt out of the launch tests' default-healthy fixture",
    "no_warm_default: opt out of the launch tests' default chat-warm fixture",
    "live_picks: opt out of the seeded SAMPLE_PICKS and resolve picks for real",
    "real_hf_client: opt out of the global hf_client.fetch_models stub (tests the client itself)",
    "download_child: opt out of the in-process download stub (drives the real child-process relay)",
    "fleet_warm_up: the test runs a real fleet warm-up thread and joins it itself",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["lilbee"]
concurrency = ["thread"]
# Generated modules are machine output, not code anyone wrote or can meaningfully
# test; measuring them says nothing about the suite. Excluded so the number stays
# a statement about hand-written code, and so regenerating cannot move it.
omit = ["src/lilbee/_generated/*"]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
fail_under = 100
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "class.*Protocol",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 100
src = ["src", "tests", "tools"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",     # pycodestyle errors
    "W",     # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",     # pyflakes
    "I",     # isort
    "UP",    # pyupgrade
    "B",     # flake8-bugbear
    "SIM",   # flake8-simplify
    "RUF",   # ruff-specific
    "S",     # flake8-bandit: security antipatterns (eval, exec, pickle, unsafe subprocess, etc.)
    "C90",   # mccabe complexity
    "N",     # pep8-naming
    "RET",   # flake8-return: consistent return semantics
    "TID",   # flake8-tidy-imports: forbid relative imports
    "PLR0911", # too many returns
    "PLR0912", # too many branches
    "PLR0915", # too many statements
    "PLR2004", # magic value used in comparison
]
# DeepSeek V3.1's tool-call markers are intentionally fullwidth (｜ U+FF5C,
# ▁ U+2581). These are the exact characters the model emits; substituting
# the ASCII look-alikes would break extraction.
allowed-confusables = ["｜", "▁"]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-bugbear]
# litestar's Body(), like Parameter() (already in ruff's B008 default allowlist),
# is a declarative parameter marker that is safe as an argument default.
extend-immutable-calls = ["litestar.params.Body"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# The namespace names of non-English wikis hold letters that look like ASCII, such as the
# Turkish dotless i; the table is the names as the wikis write them.
"src/lilbee/core/config/mediawiki_namespaces.py" = ["RUF001"]
# Test-context S-rule noise. Each of these is either a test fixture
# (hardcoded token/password literals, fake /tmp paths, 0.0.0.0 bind
# assertions), or an intentional subprocess spawn for an e2e test:
# - S101 assert (tests are built on it)
# - S104 bind-all-interfaces (testing host parsing)
# - S105/S106 hardcoded password string/arg (test fixtures)
# - S108 /tmp paths (mocked, not actual temp-file usage)
# - S311 pseudo-random (seeded generators building test data, never a secret;
#   the seed is the point, since a load test that cannot be replayed is useless)
# - S603/S607 subprocess (e2e tests spawning sys.executable)
# Test files also ignore PLR2004 (test fixtures use literal expected
# values inline; extracting them to constants hurts readability) and
# the pep8-naming rules (test helpers frequently shadow PascalCase
# class names from the system under test).
"tests/**/*.py" = [
    "S101", "S104", "S105", "S106", "S108", "S311", "S603", "S607",
    "PLR2004",
    "N802", "N806", "N818", "N817",
]
# QA matrix runner is a test framework just like tests/; same ignores apply.
"tools/qa/**/*.py" = [
    "S101", "S104", "S105", "S106", "S108", "S603", "S607",
    "PLR2004",
    "N802", "N806", "N818", "N817",
]
# Surface-QA harnesses drive the CLI/TUI/HTTP surfaces like tests do; same ignores
# (S311 for the same reason as tests: seeded fuzz walks must replay).
"scripts/qa/**/*.py" = [
    "S101", "S104", "S105", "S106", "S108", "S311", "S603", "S607",
    "PLR2004",
    "N802", "N806", "N818", "N817",
]
# Invokes the trusted `gh` CLI with controlled args to build the compat index.
"tools/build_compat_index.py" = ["S603", "S607"]
"conftest.py" = ["S101"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
check_untyped_defs = true
ignore_missing_imports = true

quality_controls.evidence: Canonical GitHub identity and retrieval timestamp
quality_controls.name: provenance

repository.description: A managed, orchestrated harness for running Claude Code as a safe, repeatable agent: hooks, guardrails, slash commands, a Jira CLI, and a cross-session handover system.
repository.name: Himmel
repository.readme:
# himmel > **A harness for Claude Code.** Audience: newcomer. The page opens with the first task for someone new to himmel; the path for running or developing himmel itself is [its own part of the Quickstart](#quickstart). ## Start here: protect one project The first thing to do with himmel is protect one project you can throw away. You install it into a spare git repository, ask Claude Code to edit a file on `main` and see the edit refused, keep the install, make one change in its own worktree, and then undo everything. **[Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md) is that trial, step by step.** Each step names the folder to run it from and what you should see, and the last step removes the install again. That one protected project is a complete result. Everything else on this page is optional and comes later: a second-brain vault, unattended runs, a fleet of parallel sessions. The [adoption trail](docs/adoption-trail.html) lays these out as levels, and each level says what it gives you, what it costs and how to turn it off. > Deciding whether it is worth it? Read [**Why himmel**](docs/why-himmel.md), > the failure modes it exists for and what each one costs. Want the design > in one read? [**System design**](docs/system-design.md) explains the parts, > one ticket's flow, the trust model and the trade-offs. Want the wiring? > [**Architecture**](docs/architecture.md) draws the enforcement layers, > handover, fleet, Jira seam and observability chain. ## What himmel is himmel is a development engine for a solo operator or a small team who works with Claude Code every day. It wraps Claude Code in hooks, guardrails, slash commands, a local Jira CLI and a handover system, so the work follows a worktree-isolated, PR-gated, Jira-tracked workflow without anyone having to remember the rules. The idea is simple: anything you would otherwise repeat by hand (checking a commit, reviewing a PR, writing down where you stopped, restarting after a usage cap) becomes a tool or a gate. Safety comes from structure, not from Claude remembering a paragraph of instructions. ## What you get The trial above shows the first of these: the edit refused on `main`, the commit gate and the worktree. The rest arrive as you add them, and the [adoption trail](docs/adoption-trail.html) says which level brings each one. - **Work carries over between sessions.** Each session leaves a plain markdown handover doc behind. A fresh session reads it and resumes where the last one stopped, with the decisions and the reasons for them intact. - **Work runs while you sleep.** `/afk-shift` hands scoped tickets to parallel agents that branch, review themselves and open PRs. When a session nears its usage cap, a usage-cap auto-relaunch schedules a relaunch with the operating system's scheduler, so a long run survives the cap. - **Mistakes are blocked, not just discouraged.** Hooks stop edits on `main`, reads of secret files, and opening a PR without a passing review, at the moment Claude tries the tool call. - **Every merge is reviewed by several agents.** `/pr-check` runs a panel of review agents plus a first pass from a second model, and the PR cannot merge until the result is clean. A finding marked critical must survive an adversarial check first, which filters out invented findings. - **It stays cheap.** A local Jira CLI replaces a Jira MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, a CLI proxy summarizes noisy command output, and each subagent gets a lean brief. All three keep the context window and the bill small. - **Memory you can read and edit.** Everything Claude remembers is a markdown file you can open. The search index on top is disposable and always points back at the file. [Memory architecture](#memory-architecture) explains how the pieces fit. - **GitHub or Bitbucket.** The worktree, PR and merge loop works the same on GitHub and Bitbucket Cloud. himmel picks the backend from each repo's `origin` remote. - **Linux and macOS.** Linux is checked on every PR, macOS on a scheduled run. Windows is not supported. Details in the [Support matrix](#support-matrix). ## How it flows

The graph walks four flows that make up most of a day with himmel. Each box lights up in order. The graph is rendered by [`scripts/docs/render-flows.py`](scripts/docs/render-flows.py); edit the script, not the image. **1. Ship a change.** Every change starts from a Jira ticket, and every commit names it. `/worktree` gives the change its own branch and directory, because nobody edits `main` directly. Hooks check each commit and push: message format, secrets, the attestation lines that say what was tested. `/pr-check` then runs the review panel. Once CI is green on the suites the change touches, the PR merges and `/clean` prunes the finished worktree. **2. Run a fleet: one supervisor session, many worker sessions.** For bigger runs, one Claude session acts as the *supervisor session*. It plans the work and starts *worker sessions*, other Claude sessions that each own one ticket, one worktree and one PR. A worker session reports back with short status markers (`LIVE`, `READY`) and never merges on its own. The supervisor session checks the PR (and can ask an independent judge subagent for a second opinion), writes a GO file (merge approval) to sign off, and the worker session merges through `merge-on-green.sh`. The [glossary](docs/glossary.md) defines console, leg, judge and the rest. **3. Carry work across sessions.** A session that has made decisions writes them into a handover doc with `/handover`. The doc lives in your handover state repo, not in the project, so it survives anything that happens to the session. If the session hits its usage cap, himmel arms a relaunch. The next session runs `/handover-resume`, reads the doc, and continues where the last one stopped. **4. Find what you already know.** Before improvising, a session looks up what is already known. Claude Code's per-project `MEMORY.md` is a short index that routes a keyword to a topic note. `qmd` searches the markdown itself (notes, handovers, docs) by keyword and meaning. `graphify` answers questions about how the code fits together. Each hop ends at a real file, and a lesson learned on the way is written back to memory for the next session. The commands behind flow 1: ```bash /worktree feat/my-thing # isolated branch + worktree (never edit on main) # … work with Claude in the worktree … git commit && git push # hooks gate the message, secrets and attestation lines /pr-check # review panel; clears the merge gate when clean gh pr create # then merge once CI is green and the PR is approved /clean # prune merged worktrees /handover # write down where you stopped ``` Going unattended: ```bash /afk-shift --limit 5 # five scoped tickets to parallel agents, each ending in a PR /stop # ask an overnight run to halt gracefully ``` [`docs/daily-loop.md`](docs/daily-loop.md) walks flow 1 end to end and explains every hook at the moment it fires. [`docs/configuration.md`](docs/configuration.md) lists every gate, knob and off switch in one place. A language model (or a new session) should start from [`llms.txt`](llms.txt), the machine-readable map of the repo. ## Quickstart himmel is a harness *for* [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), so install Claude Code first: `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`. There are two ways in: 1. **Add himmel to a project** (newcomer; the usual case). This brings over the portable core: hooks, guardrails, the worktree workflow and the marketplace plugins and skills. Do the trial in [`docs/getting-started.md`](docs/getting-started.md) on a spare project first. The [adoption trail](docs/adoption-trail.html) (also at [yotamleo-org.github.io/Himmel/adoption-trail.html](https://yotamleo-org.github.io/Himmel/adoption-trail.html)) shows what each later level of adoption changes. 2. **Run or develop himmel itself** (contributor). This path has more prerequisites, and the rest of this section covers it. **Prerequisites.** `bash`, `git`, `node`, `npm`, `bun`, `python3`, `jq`, `gh` and `mktemp`; `scripts/setup.sh` checks for them first and stops with install hints if one is missing. You also need one of `uv`, `pipx` or an installed `pre-commit`: setup uses it to install `pre-commit` and then wires the git hooks. `bun` runs the handover resume resolver, the qmd search index, the Telegram bridge and the vault triage tools. Per-platform install steps are in [`docs/setup/new-machine.md`](docs/setup/new-machine.md). **Linux, from the release tarball** (checksummed and pre-built: no clone, no `npm install`): ```bash V=X.Y.Z # a release that ships the tarball: https://github.com/yotamleo-org/Himmel/releases curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/yotamleo-org/Himmel/releases/download/v$V/himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz" curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/yotamleo-org/Himmel/releases/download/v$V/himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz.sha256" sha256sum -c "himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz.sha256" \ && mkdir -p ~/.local/share/himmel/"$V" \ && tar -xzf "himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz" -C ~/.local/share/himmel/"$V" --strip-components=1 \ && ln -sfn "$V" ~/.local/share/himmel/current \ && node ~/.local/share/himmel/current/scripts/himmelctl/bin.js install --scope user ``` The `&&` chain matters: if the tarball does not match its published `.sha256`, `sha256sum -c` fails and nothing is extracted or installed. With `gh` you can also check that this repo's CI built it: `gh attestation verify himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz -R yotamleo/Himmel`. CI builds the tarball on each `v*` tag ([`release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml)). Each release unpacks into its own `~/.local/share/himmel//` (no root needed), and `~/.local/share/himmel/current` points at the live one. `himmelctl install` wires everything through `current` and puts a `himmelctl` launcher in `~/.local/bin`. To upgrade, run `himmelctl update`. It downloads the latest release, verifies it, unpacks it next to the old one and only then switches `current`, so a failed download changes nothing. To roll back, point `current` at the previous version: `ln -sfn ~/.local/share/himmel/current`. After `himmelctl uninstall`, deleting `~/.local/share/himmel` removes every version. An older install that unpacked straight into `~/.local/share/himmel` predates this layout: move it aside and install once with the recipe above. **Linux or macOS, from a clone:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/yotamleo-org/Himmel himmel cd himmel node scripts/himmelctl/bin.js install ``` No node on the machine yet? Run `bash scripts/himmelctl/bootstrap.sh` first, then `install`. The wizard runs `scripts/setup.sh` under the hood; call that directly for a manual or CI install. **Environment.** Set these in the shell that launches Claude. luna, Telegram, hermes and Jira are all optional; the harness runs without them. | Variable | Required? | Notes | |----------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------| | `USER_SLUG` | recommended | Your kebab-case handle, e.g. `jane-doe`. Names your handover bucket (`handovers//`) and worktree dirs. If unset, it is derived from `git config user.name`; setup fails only if both are unset. | | `JIRA_PROJECT_KEY` | only for Jira | e.g. `HIMMEL`. The project the CLI creates and queries issues in. | | `JIRA_BASE_URL` | only for Jira | Your Atlassian site, e.g. `https://your-site.atlassian.net`. | | `JIRA_API_TOKEN` + `JIRA_EMAIL` | only for Jira | API-token credentials. Never commit them; `.env` is gitignored. | | `HANDOVER_DIR` | recommended | Path to your external handover repo. Or leave it unset and run `/handover-setup` once. Until one of the two is done there is no handover root, and handover commands stop with a clear message instead of writing to the wrong place. | The Jira CLI needs only those four Jira variables, no cloud ID. `JIRA_CLOUD_ID` is only for the optional Atlassian MCP server. The full list is in [`.env.example`](.env.example). Check the install: ```bash node scripts/jira/dist/index.js list # talk to Jira gh auth status # talk to GitHub pre-commit run --all-files # all hooks green ``` Then run one full loop (worktree, commit, PR, merge, `/clean`, `/handover`) with [`docs/daily-loop.md`](docs/daily-loop.md) open beside you. ## Support matrix himmel is developed on Linux and macOS. **Windows (Git Bash, WSL) is not supported.** The Windows code paths are still in the tree and Windows issues are welcome, but nothing about Windows is claimed as working. | Tier | Platforms | What it promises | |---|---|---| | **Supported** | Linux | Checked on every PR as a required check ([CI runs on `main`](https://github.com/yotamleo-org/Himmel/actions/workflows/ci.yml?query=branch%3Amain)). The adopter round trip is verified. | | **Supported** | macOS | Checked on a scheduled run twice a week, not on every PR ([scheduled macOS runs](https://github.com/yotamleo-org/Himmel/actions/workflows/macos-cadence.yml?query=event%3Aschedule)). A macOS-only failure is fixed as its own change ([`docs/internals/testing.md`](docs/internals/testing.md)). | | **Not supported** | Windows (Git Bash), WSL | Code paths exist but are unverified: no CI gate, no guarantee. | **Install channels:** | Channel | Status | |---|---| | Release tarball (`himmel--linux.tar.gz` + `.sha256`) | **Supported** on Linux: the recipe above. A fresh machine installing from it is tested end to end. | | `git clone` + `himmelctl install` | **Supported** on Linux and macOS. | | Plugin marketplace (`marketplace/plugins/*`, one directory per plugin) | **Supported.** Installed, updated and removed by Claude Code itself (`claude plugin install/update/uninstall`), not by `himmelctl`. Includes [`himmel-ops`](marketplace/plugins/himmel-ops/README.md) (skills that load when a guardrail stops you and explain the way out), [`himmel-bus`](docs/himmel-bus.md) (a local message bus between sessions, early) and [`luna-correlate`](marketplace/plugins/luna-correlate/README.md) (an opt-in, offline health-factor correlation MCP). | | AUR (`himmel`, recipe in [`packaging/aur/`](packaging/aur/)) | **Supported after the first AUR push** (Arch). `pacman` installs to `/opt/himmel`; each user then runs `himmelctl install --scope user`, and `himmelctl update` defers to `pacman -Syu`. To remove: `himmelctl uninstall` for each user, then `pacman -R himmel`. | | brew (Linux tap) | Not supported. Reconsidered if a tap shared with macOS becomes worthwhile. | | nix, deb, rpm | Not supported. Reconsidered when users ask for a given channel. | New shell scripts target bash and stay bash 3.2-safe, so they run on macOS's default bash. See [`docs/internals/harness-compat.md`](docs/internals/harness-compat.md) for how himmel behaves under other harnesses. ## Memory architecture There are two broad ways to give an AI agent memory. The first is a **memory backend**: software pulls facts out of your conversations and files, stores them in a separate database (usually as vector embeddings), and later retrieves the closest-matching facts *instead of* the files they came from. Writing about agent memory sometimes calls this "Camp 1". The second is a **context substrate** ("Camp 2"): the files themselves are the memory. The agent reads them, reasons over them and writes back to them. Any index exists only to find the right file faster. himmel is firmly in the second camp. The reason is that a single operator is the source of truth and should be able to open, read and fix what the agent remembers. Pulling one fact out of a file throws away the context that made it useful: the links, the surrounding decisions, the reason it was written. A memory backend wins when the corpus is too large to read and nobody needs to inspect it, as in enterprise document search. That is not himmel's case. What the memory is made of today, all plain files: - **Auto-memory.** Claude Code keeps a per-project memory folder. himmel uses its `MEMORY.md` as a short index that *routes*: one line per theme, each pointing to a topic note that holds the detail. A session reads the index, then only the notes it needs. - **Handover state.** Each piece of work has a markdown handover doc in your handover state repo (`$HANDOVER_DIR`): what was done, what was decided, what comes next. This is how work survives the end of a session. The state can live in your own repo or in a separate handover repo; see the [handover system](docs/internals/handover-system.md). - **The luna vault (optional).** An Obsidian vault built from [`templates/luna-second-brain/`](templates/luna-second-brain/) holds notes, web clippings and daily entries that Claude reads and writes like any other markdown. Two search tools sit on top. Neither replaces a file: - **[qmd](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tobilu/qmd)** is a local search engine over the markdown, using keyword ranking (BM25) and vectors. It returns a pointer to the source file, never a fact in its place. The index can be deleted and rebuilt at any time. That is the line between the two camps: not whether embeddings are used, but whether you get the file back. - **graphify** builds a knowledge graph of the code (which file and function relates to which) and answers structure questions with `graphify query` and `graphify explain`. The graph is rebuilt from the source on a schedule. A data-egress fence ([`docs/internals/egress-matrix.md`](docs/internals/egress-matrix.md)) decides which files may reach which extraction provider. ### Companion vault tooling (optional) If you run the vault in Obsidian, himmel ships and pins the tools to operate it. None of them is needed by the core harness. - **[obsidian-triage](marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/README.md)** (part of himmel) turns an Obsidian Web Clipper inbox into a knowledge base that keeps itself tidy: `/harvest-clips`, `/triage-clips`, `/synthesize-clips`, `/archive-clips`. - **qmd** reaches Claude as an MCP server (`qmd@qmd`). The standalone CLI installs from himmel's qmd fork with `bash scripts/lib/qmd-bin.sh install`, which setup runs for you. - **[claude-obsidian](https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian)**, pinned to an upstream release tag: skills to ingest, query and save notes, and to lint vault health (`wiki-lint`). - **[obsidian (kepano)](https://github.com/kepano/obsidian-skills)**, pinned: the `obsidian-markdown` skill for Obsidian-flavored markdown. A weekly vault-health pass (`/obsidian-health`, Sundays at 04:00) is scheduled by [`pipeline-cadence`](.claude/commands/pipeline-cadence.md). ## Features Every feature has one doc that owns its detail; the full map is [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md). **Core loop and enforcement** - Worktree isolation with `/worktree`, `/clean`, `/clean_garden`: [`docs/commands-catalog.md`](docs/commands-catalog.md) and [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) (`## WORKFLOWS`) - Pre-commit and Claude tool-call guardrail hooks, and the multi-agent PR review (`/pr-check`) that gates every merge: [`docs/internals/enforcement.md`](docs/internals/enforcement.md) - Handover system (multi-repo registry, auto-branch, PR, flush): [`docs/internals/handover-system.md`](docs/internals/handover-system.md) - Collision preflight before starting a session: `bash scripts/handover/queue-lock.sh preflight [file...]` warns (exit 20) when a file you intend to touch is already changed in another live session's checkout; read-only, `queue-lock.sh` header lists the contract - AFK (unattended) mode runs (`/afk-shift`, `/stop` to halt): [`docs/handover/afk-mode.md`](docs/handover/afk-mode.md) **Lifecycle and delegation** - `himmelctl` install, update and uninstall: [`docs/setup/updating.md`](docs/setup/updating.md) - Delegation across Claude model tiers, plus optional GLM and Codex lanes, listed live by `/lanes`: [`docs/tooling-catalog.md`](docs/tooling-catalog.md) - Cloud lane (`claude --cloud` sessions on your fork): [`docs/setup/cloud-environment.md`](docs/setup/cloud-environment.md) - Watchers that cost almost no tokens: `/morning-report` (git, GitHub and Jira state) and the `check-ci` merge-gate watcher: [`docs/commands-catalog.md`](docs/commands-catalog.md) - Test VMs (osboxes, Multipass) driven by `/vm`: [`docs/setup/vms.md`](docs/setup/vms.md) **Jira and forge** - Jira CLI, a token-cheap local replacement for an MCP server: [`scripts/jira/`](scripts/jira/) and [`docs/internals/jira-plugin.md`](docs/internals/jira-plugin.md) - GitHub and Bitbucket Cloud, detected from `origin`: [`scripts/bitbucket/`](scripts/bitbucket/) and [`plugins/himmel-gh/`](plugins/himmel-gh/) **Knowledge (optional)** - Vault capture and the clip pipeline (harvest, triage, synthesize, archive): [`marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/README.md`](marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/README.md) - graphify and qmd: see [Memory architecture](#memory-architecture) **Comms** - Telegram bridge (arm a session, check status, chat from your phone): [`docs/telegram-bridge.md`](docs/telegram-bridge.md) ## Who is this for Claude Code use tends to grow through four stages: 1. **Vanilla**: Claude Code as it ships. Boris Cherny, one of its creators, has described his own setup as "surprisingly vanilla". 2. **Customized**: your own skills and slash commands. 3. **Orchestrated**: parallel agents and a harness around them. 4. **Autonomous**: scheduled runs that work unattended, around the clock. himmel is built for stages 3 and 4. If you are happy at stage 1, and many excellent engineers are, you do not need it. It earns its complexity once you run several sessions in parallel, want work done overnight, or want work to build on itself across sessions without re-explaining the context each time. ## Setup details - **A new machine, step by step:** [`docs/setup/new-machine.md`](docs/setup/new-machine.md) (required environment and per-platform notes). - **Adopting himmel in your own repo:** `git clone https://github.com/yotamleo-org/Himmel himmel`, then `node himmel/scripts/himmelctl/bin.js install --scope project` (or `--scope user`). Leave out `--scope` to walk the wizard. What each scope and install profile brings, and the checklist for a repo that is not himmel: [`docs/setup/install.md`](docs/setup/install.md). Coming from an older install: [`docs/setup/migrating.md`](docs/setup/migrating.md). - **Updating:** `/himmel-update` updates the harness (a `git pull` plus a marketplace re-sync; Claude Code's own `autoUpdate` does not deliver himmel). `/luna-upgrade` upgrades a companion vault separately. - **Uninstalling:** `node scripts/himmelctl/bin.js uninstall`. Preview it first with `uninstall --dry-run`, which touches nothing. It removes himmel's wiring and keeps your state unless you pass `--purge-state` ([details](docs/setup/install.md#uninstalling)). All of this in full: [`docs/setup/updating.md`](docs/setup/updating.md). - **Global Claude Code config** (`~/.claude/`): [`docs/setup/global-claude-md.md`](docs/setup/global-claude-md.md). - **Test VMs:** [`docs/setup/vms.md`](docs/setup/vms.md). - **Status line:** a pinned [claude-hud](marketplace/plugins/claude-hud/VENDORED.md) shows live session and cost data ([`docs/tooling-catalog.md`](docs/tooling-catalog.md)). - **Security review** before shipping code changes: [`docs/security-review.md`](docs/security-review.md). ## Docs site (local preview) `bash scripts/docs-site/serve.sh` builds `docs/` with Starlight and serves it on loopback only: open `http://127.0.0.1:4321/Himmel/`. Needs Node 22.22+ and network on first run (`npm ci` in `site/`). ## Contributing The workflow is in [`docs/contributing.md`](docs/contributing.md). In short: 1. All work goes through a PR; `main` is protected. 2. Conventional commits with the ticket in the subject: `type(scope): [PROJ-123] message`. 3. One worktree per branch (`/worktree /`); never edit on `main`. 4. Pre-commit and pre-push hooks must pass. 5. A new shell script comes with a smoke test (`scripts//test-.sh`). ## Project conventions Commits follow Conventional Commits with a Jira ticket in the subject, and the pre-commit hooks enforce the format. Worktrees live under `.claude/worktrees/` and branches are named `/` (`feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`). Branch protection, force-push gates, platform attestation and the rules for headless Claude runs are all in [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md). ## License himmel is licensed under the MIT License; see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). The vendored fork `marketplace/plugins/telegram-himmel` keeps its upstream **Apache-2.0** license; see its `LICENSE` file. `scripts/cr/floor-reviewer.md` is a modified copy of the Apache-2.0 `code-reviewer` agent from `anthropics/claude-plugins-official` (see `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`). Third-party attribution for vendored bundles and the dependency-license audit (clean, fully permissive) is in [`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md).

name: CI

on:
  # PR gating (HIMMEL-594): the cheap ubuntu-only jobs run on every PR so a
  # non-conventional commit, a secret, a shellcheck warning, or a failing shell
  # suite blocks merge. Every job here is ubuntu only: Windows support is
  # dropped (HIMMEL-5729) and there is no dispatch input that widens a matrix
  # (HIMMEL-3853), so neither a PR nor a manual dispatch can occupy a paid leg. macOS is not in
  # this file at all (HIMMEL-3902): it runs on its own twice-weekly workflow,
  # macos-cadence.yml, so a macOS red can never turn this run -- or main -- red.
  # `shell-unit` itself (HIMMEL-2872) is the aggregating gate over that
  # matrix — see its own comment block below.
  pull_request:
  # HIMMEL-5113: there is NO `push` trigger. Main used to run this workflow on
  # every merge (~52 runs/day, about half cancelled as superseded, ~2,300 runner
  # hours on the green ones alone) and those runs competed with PR runs for the
  # account's 20 runner slots. Post-merge verification (HIMMEL-511) is now the
  # main-sweep cron below. Trade-off: a break that reached main surfaces up to
  # a nominal 7 h later and spans every merge since the previous run; the cron run prints
  # that range (step `Merge range since the previous main run`) and
  # main-sweep-red.yml names it in the main-red issue.
  # A run at an exact sha (a tag cut, a bisect) is a manual dispatch:
  #   gh workflow run ci.yml --ref main
  # then check-ci.sh / cut-tag.sh read that run. A dispatch takes no inputs on
  # purpose (HIMMEL-3853): a per-PR all-OS dispatch held 14 of the account's 20
  # concurrent job slots on 2026-09-29. It runs the ubuntu-only matrix.
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    # Nightly, UTC: the only run with guard-corpus-full. Every nightly-only gate
    # below keys on THIS string via github.event.schedule, because the
    # main-sweep cron is also a `schedule` event and must stay ubuntu-only.
    # SUITE_TIER_MODE=all runs on every non-pull_request run (HIMMEL-6598).
    - cron: '17 7 * * *'
    # Main sweep (HIMMEL-5113), UTC, ubuntu-only, SUITE_TIER_MODE=all (HIMMEL-6598), the shape the
    # per-merge push run had. Nominal cadence: 01:43, 08:43, 15:43 and 22:43,
    # i.e. gaps of 7 h, 7 h, 7 h and 3 h -- cron cannot express an exact 7 h
    # period because 24 is not a multiple of 7 (`*/7` fires at 00, 07, 14, 21 and
    # then resets to 00). That is the cron STRING gap only: GitHub fires schedules
    # late on this repo (the 17 7 nightly was created 4-9 h late over 40 days),
    # so the real gap can reach ~11-12 h. Tune the hours here;
    # test-ci-main-cron.sh holds the nominal max gap at 7 h.
    - cron: '43 1,8,15,22 * * *'

permissions:
  contents: read

# HIMMEL-3217 / HIMMEL-3226: a newer run cancels the run it supersedes -- on
# 2026-09-19 stale runs kept the Actions queue at 5+ and leg PR runs waited
# 25-40 min. Two DISJOINT groups (a workflow has one top-level block):
#   pull_request -> ci-pr-<PR number>: a PR's newer push cancels that PR's
#                   older run, and never another PR's;
#   everything else (both crons, workflow_dispatch) -> ci-<run_id>: unique to
#                   the run, so a sweep / the nightly / a dispatch is never
#                   cancelled nor queued behind anything. The shared
#                   push-to-main group (HIMMEL-3841 slice E, HIMMEL-5036) went
#                   with the push trigger: sweeps are hours apart and a
#                   ~1h45m sweep cannot normally meet the next one. A delayed
#                   schedule or a manual dispatch can overlap one, and then the
#                   runs complete out of order (main-sweep-red-issue.sh keeps
#                   the newest run's verdict by run id).
# cancel-in-progress is scoped to pull_request alone, so it stays inert for the
# run_id groups. A cancelled run only ever belongs to a superseded head: the
# required checks (incl. the `shell-unit` aggregator) are evaluated on the PR's
# current head, whose own run this never cancels.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.pull_request.number) || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  # HIMMEL-5524: which jobs can this PR's diff affect? A pull_request spends
  # about 30 jobs and queues behind the account's runner cap, so a docs-only or
  # single-script PR waited 45-60 min for jobs whose inputs it never touched.
  # This job (pull_request only) runs the BASE commit's scripts/ci/pr-plan.sh
  # (the base's pr-job-gates.txt, the base's impacted-selection.sh) and exposes
  # one run_<group> output per gated job. Every gated job reads it FAIL-OPEN:
  # `!cancelled()` plus "skip only when the plan succeeded and said false", so a
  # plan that failed, was skipped (push, schedule, dispatch run everything) or
  # printed nothing runs the job. A trust-path diff, an unknown path, a base
  # that predates the planner or any selector error is all-true (see pr-plan.sh).
  # A skipped non-matrix job reports `skipped`, which satisfies a required
  # check; the matrix jobs (node-suites, bun-suites) stay started and skip their
  # STEPS, because a skipped matrix job leaves its required names pending.

    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 13 # p95 ~70s (the 60 s debounce sleep + checkout + plan); kept 13 for sleep + slow-runner headroom
    outputs:
      run_node_suites: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.run_node_suites }}
      run_jira_cli_smoke: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.run_jira_cli_smoke }}
      run_guardrail_matrices: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.run_guardrail_matrices }}
      run_git_env_scrub: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.run_git_env_scrub }}
      run_bwk_gate: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.run_bwk_gate }}
      run_plugin_version_bump: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.run_plugin_version_bump }}
      run_deps_audit: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.run_deps_audit }}
      shards: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.shards }}
      absent_shards: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.absent_shards }}
      shard_total: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.shard_total }}
    steps:
      # Debounce. Every shell-unit shard needs this job, and a follow-up push
      # within ~1 min of the last one cancels a run whose shards already took
      # runners. A newer push cancels this run while it sleeps here, so no shard
      # starts. A PR's first run (opened) has no earlier push to absorb, so it
      # does not sleep. Cost: 1 runner-minute and 1 minute of latency per later push.
      # test-ci-push-concurrency.sh holds the 45-90 s window and the opened skip.

          persist-credentials: false

          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}

          set -o pipefail
          tools="$RUNNER_TEMP/plan-tools"
          mkdir -p "$tools"
          base=""
          [ "$BASE_REF" = "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" ] && base="$BASE_SHA"
          # The planner, its input list and the selector come from the BASE, never
          # the PR's own edited copy. Absent at base -> empty plan -> every job runs.

            : > "$tools/plan.out"

          grep -E '^(mode|run_[a-z_]+)=[a-z]+$' "$tools/plan.out" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" || true
      # HIMMEL-5649 / HIMMEL-5556: how many shell-unit shards (at most
      # vars.CI_MAX_SHARDS, 20 unset) the selection needs, sized off the duration
      # ledger. Asked once, here, under
      # the SAME selection env the shards' run step gets, so a small selection
      # takes few runners and a shard with nothing to run never takes one. An
      # empty output (this step failed) means all 8 start, see shell-unit-shard.
      - id: shards

        env:

          PR_BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          CI_MAX_SHARDS: ${{ vars.CI_MAX_SHARDS }}
        run: |
          # A pull_request is never the nightly: tier is always pr here. The
          # shards' SUITE_MANIFEST makes their runner decide the selection even
          # with no base (mode full runs every tier), so the list asks with one.
          export SUITE_TIER_MODE=pr GUARD_CORPUS_TIER=fast SUITE_CHANGED_SINCE="$PR_BASE_SHA" SUITE_MANIFEST="$RUNNER_TEMP/plan-manifest.txt"
          if [ "$PR_BASE_REF" = "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" ]; then export SUITE_IMPACTED_FROM_BASE="$PR_BASE_SHA"; fi
          bash scripts/ci/plan-shards.sh "${CI_MAX_SHARDS:-20}" . > "$RUNNER_TEMP/shards.out" || : > "$RUNNER_TEMP/shards.out"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/shards.out"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/shards.out" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # HIMMEL-5675: the short checks run as step groups of this ONE job, so they
  # take one runner and one setup instead of eight (19 of 42 PR jobs finished
  # under 60 s, each paying 5-30 s of setup and a queue slot). A group is the
  # steps whose id is <group> or <group>__<x>; every step runs under
  # !cancelled(), so one red group never hides another. The group's output is
  # 'pass' only when the shared steps, the closing `finished` step and each of
  # its own steps succeeded or were skipped by a gate; anything else, a
  # cancelled or timed-out job included, leaves it 'fail' or empty. Each old job
  # name below stays as a sentinel carrying its required context: skipped

  # result, so a ci-quick that timed out, whichever result a timeout reports,
  # still fails them. test-ci-quick.sh holds the shape.
  #
  # Not changed, on purpose:
  # - ci-quick waits behind the plan job (and its debounce sleep) because its
  #   steps gate on plan's run_* outputs. Taking it out from behind plan drops
  #   that gating, to save latency only.
  # - The groups share one workspace, so a group that edits the tree could turn
  #   a later one red (a false red, never a false green). The one destructive
  #   group, doc-invariants, runs last (test-ci-quick.sh Q5); a separate
  #   checkout per group would put back the setup cost this fold removed.
  ci-quick:
    needs: plan
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Runs in the prebuilt CI image (docs/internals/ci-image.md). A fork or
    # dependabot[bot] run cannot pull the private package, so it gets '' (no
    # container) and the setup steps gated on !job.container.id install the
    # same tools on the host.

    # --privileged: bwrap and unshare need user namespaces inside the container.

      image: ${{ !(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository || github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]') && (vars.CI_IMAGE || 'ghcr.io/yotamleo-org/himmel-ci@sha256:6c7a604e4c615486e62303d70039361775a44b1ca3c04eb098a7b06cbbd85009') || '' }} # env-literal-ok: the CI image's own GHCR path, pinned by digest

        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ github.token }}
      options: --init --user 1001 --privileged

      contents: read
      packages: read
    timeout-minutes: 30 # p95 sum of the folded jobs ~250s plus one setup; 30 bounds a hung group

      secret-scan: ${{ steps.finished.outcome == 'success' && steps.checkout.outcome == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.setup-node.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.secret-scan.outcome) && 'pass' || 'fail' }}
      bwk-awk-mktemp-gate: ${{ steps.finished.outcome == 'success' && steps.checkout.outcome == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.setup-node.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.bwk-awk-mktemp-gate.outcome) && 'pass' || 'fail' }}
      unchecked-mktemp-range: ${{ steps.finished.outcome == 'success' && steps.checkout.outcome == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.setup-node.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.unchecked-mktemp-range.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.unchecked-mktemp-range__read-sinks.outcome) && 'pass' || 'fail' }}
      commit-lint: ${{ steps.finished.outcome == 'success' && steps.checkout.outcome == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.setup-node.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.commit-lint.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.commit-lint__platforms.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.commit-lint__security.outcome) && 'pass' || 'fail' }}
      jira-cli-smoke: ${{ steps.finished.outcome == 'success' && steps.checkout.outcome == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.setup-node.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.jira-cli-smoke__npm.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.jira-cli-smoke.outcome) && 'pass' || 'fail' }}
      guardrail-matrices: ${{ steps.finished.outcome == 'success' && steps.checkout.outcome == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.setup-node.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.guardrail-matrices.outcome) && 'pass' || 'fail' }}
      claude-startup: ${{ steps.finished.outcome == 'success' && steps.checkout.outcome == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.setup-node.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.claude-startup__bun.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.claude-startup__bun-path.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.claude-startup__cli.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.claude-startup__userns.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.claude-startup.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.claude-startup__mock-turn.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.claude-startup__apt-image.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.claude-startup__apt-cache.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.claude-startup__apt.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.claude-startup__consult.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.claude-startup__hook-smoke.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.claude-startup__shfmt.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.claude-startup__live-turn.outcome) && 'pass' || 'fail' }}
      doc-invariants: ${{ steps.finished.outcome == 'success' && steps.checkout.outcome == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.setup-node.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__dev.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__guard.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__self.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__desc-cap.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__positional.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__catalog.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__secrets-doc.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__llms.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__terms.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__hermetic.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__stage.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__agents-md.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__debrand.outcome) && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), steps.doc-invariants__lanes.outcome) && 'pass' || 'fail' }}
    # The image sets no locale (POSIX counts bytes); C.UTF-8 is the host runner's.
    env:
      LANG: C.UTF-8
      LC_ALL: C.UTF-8
      CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION: '2.1.296'
    # A container's default run shell is sh; this is the host runner's default.
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash -e {0}
    steps:
      # Full history: commit-lint, unchecked-mktemp-range and doc-guard walk the
      # PR range. This checks out and executes contributor code, so the token is
      # not persisted into .git/config.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        id: checkout
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        id: setup-node
        if: ${{ !job.container.id }}
        with:
          node-version: '22.23.4'
      - id: secret-scan
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: |
          bash scripts/ci/check-no-secrets.sh
          bash scripts/ci/check-actions-pinned.sh
          bash scripts/ci/check-ci-install-locks.sh
      - id: bwk-awk-mktemp-gate
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_bwk_gate == 'false') }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash scripts/ci/run-unchecked-mktemp-under-bwk.sh
      - id: unchecked-mktemp-range
        name: No unchecked mktemp capture added anywhere in the PR range
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash scripts/hooks/check-unchecked-mktemp.sh --range --merge-ref "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
      # HIMMEL-6037 / HIMMEL-6621: newly added shell that reads an argv/env-named
      # file with no allowlist (the PR 2878 class). The runtime half of the leak
      # check, the honeytoken HOME, runs inside every shell-unit shard.
      - id: unchecked-mktemp-range__read-sinks
        name: No host-file read sink added without an allowlist
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash scripts/ci/check-host-file-read-sinks.sh --range --merge-ref "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
      - id: commit-lint
        name: Lint commit messages in the PR range
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        env:
          TICKET_ID_REQUIRED: '1'
          JIRA_PROJECT_KEY: HIMMEL
          TICKET_ID_TRUSTED_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            bash scripts/ci/check-commit-range.sh --merge-ref "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          else
            bash scripts/ci/check-commit-range.sh
          fi
      # HIMMEL-5423: the attestation trailers are checked only at pre-push and in
      # ready-check, both skipped by a --no-verify commit. These re-run the SAME
      # pre-push gates over the PR range; the wrapper builds a branch-shaped
      # scratch clone (the hooks no-op on a detached merge ref) and keeps only
      # the PR's FIRST commit message, the rule CLAUDE.md states.
      - id: commit-lint__platforms
        name: First commit carries Platforms tested on shell/script diffs
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        env:
          TICKET_ID_REQUIRED: '1'
          JIRA_PROJECT_KEY: HIMMEL
          TICKET_ID_TRUSTED_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
        run: bash scripts/ci/check-hooks-on-pr-range.sh --first-commit -- scripts/hooks/check-platforms-tested.sh
      - id: commit-lint__security
        name: First commit carries Security reviewed on non-docs code
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        env:
          TICKET_ID_REQUIRED: '1'
          JIRA_PROJECT_KEY: HIMMEL
          TICKET_ID_TRUSTED_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
        run: bash scripts/ci/check-hooks-on-pr-range.sh --first-commit -- scripts/hooks/check-security-reviewed.sh
      # HIMMEL-3616: the PR-title lint (the squash merge makes the title
      # main's commit subject) lives in its own workflow,
      # .github/workflows/pr-title-lint.yml — not here. commit-lint's
      # `pull_request:` trigger has no `edited` type, so a step here would
      # never re-run when a title is fixed via `gh pr edit --title`
      # (judge J1284O F2); it also never threaded the PR author into
      # TICKET_ID_AUTHOR, so the dependabot[bot] exemption never applied to
      # a title (judge J1284O F1).
      - id: jira-cli-smoke__npm
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_jira_cli_smoke == 'false') }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts
        working-directory: scripts/jira
      - id: jira-cli-smoke
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_jira_cli_smoke == 'false') }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash scripts/ci/jira-cli-smoke.sh
      - id: guardrail-matrices
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_guardrail_matrices == 'false') }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash scripts/hooks/check-guardrail-matrices.sh
      # claude-startup is ungated (trust judge j2543g): the hook chain it starts
      # executes scripts outside any gate group, so it runs on every PR like main.
      # HIMMEL-4412: the project's SessionStart/Subagent hooks run `bun`; a runner
      # without it makes them exit 127 and the hook smoke correctly reports a failing hook.
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        id: claude-startup__bun
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && !job.container.id }}
        with:
          bun-version-file: .bun-version
      # The mock sandbox runs claude under a scrubbed PATH (claude, node, /usr/local/bin,
      # /usr/bin, /bin), so setup-bun's ~/.bun/bin must be linked into one of those.
      - id: claude-startup__bun-path
        name: Put bun on the scrubbed PATH
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && !job.container.id }}
        run: sudo ln -sf "$(command -v bun)" /usr/local/bin/bun
      - id: claude-startup__cli
        name: Install the pinned claude CLI
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        # HIMMEL-7092: installed from .github/claude-cli/package-lock.json (sha512 per
        # package) with no install scripts; the native binary is the locked platform
        # package's own file. /usr/local is root-owned in the image and the runner alike.
        run: |
          npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund --prefix .github/claude-cli
          sudo install -m 0755 .github/claude-cli/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64/claude /usr/local/bin/claude
          claude --version
      # ubuntu-24.04 refuses unprivileged user namespaces by default (AppArmor);
      # the suite needs `unshare -rn` and fails closed without it.
      - id: claude-startup__userns
        name: Allow unprivileged user namespaces
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0 || true
      - id: claude-startup
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash scripts/testing/test-fakekey-claude-startup.sh
      # HIMMEL-4411: a full scripted turn (text, Bash tool_use, tool_result) against
      # scripts/testing/mock-anthropic. The suite also asserts the installed CLI
      # equals CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION, so a version drift fails loudly here.
      - id: claude-startup__mock-turn
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash scripts/testing/test-claude-mock-turn.sh
      # HIMMEL-4412: two "a hook that fails open" smokes on the same mock. MOCK-BACKED:
      # they prove Claude Code enforces the consult sandbox and that the project hook
      # chain fires clean in a real session; neither is evidence of real-model behaviour.
      # The consult sandbox needs bubblewrap and socat on the runner.
      - id: claude-startup__apt-image
        name: Record runner image (apt cache key)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && !job.container.id }}
        run: echo "APT_IMAGE=${ImageVersion:-unknown}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - id: claude-startup__apt-cache
        name: Cache apt debs (consult)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && !job.container.id }}
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/apt-archives
          key: apt-${{ runner.os }}-${{ env.APT_IMAGE }}-consult-${{ hashFiles('.github/scripts/apt-install.sh') }}
      - id: claude-startup__apt
        name: Install the consult sandbox prerequisites
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && !job.container.id }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash .github/scripts/apt-install.sh bubblewrap socat
      - id: claude-startup__consult
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash scripts/testing/test-mock-consult-sandbox.sh
      - id: claude-startup__hook-smoke
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash scripts/testing/test-mock-hook-smoke.sh
      # The live turn denies `git stash drop` through block-git-stash.sh, which reads
      # the command with shfmt; without it the deny text names shfmt, not the stash.
      # Same pinned, sha-verified release as the shell-unit job; keep in lockstep.
      # The sandboxed claude run rebuilds PATH from /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
      # (fakekey-claude.sh), so the binary goes to /usr/local/bin, not GITHUB_PATH.
      - id: claude-startup__shfmt
        name: Install pinned shfmt (live-turn deny text)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: |
          shfmt_ver=3.14.1
          shfmt_sha=76e77641faa025814b77f153b29796b8e6fa2fca03e0c76a691608b86c7ea7bf
          curl -sSfL "https://github.com/mvdan/sh/releases/download/v${shfmt_ver}/shfmt_v${shfmt_ver}_linux_amd64" -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/shfmt"
          echo "${shfmt_sha}  $RUNNER_TEMP/shfmt" | sha256sum -c -
          sudo install -m 0755 "$RUNNER_TEMP/shfmt" /usr/local/bin/shfmt
      - id: claude-startup__live-turn
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash scripts/testing/test-mock-hook-live-turn.sh
      # doc-invariants goes LAST: it touches .himmel-dev and its staging step
      # leaves HEAD on an unborn orphan branch.
      - id: doc-invariants__dev
        name: Enable the himmel-dev gates in this checkout
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: touch .himmel-dev
      # HIMMEL-5423 — doc-guard (a command/skill ADDED without its catalog
      # entry) ran only in pre-commit and pre-push, so a --no-verify commit
      # skipped it. Runs the same `check-doc-guard.sh --pre-push` over the PR
      # range. MUST stay ABOVE the destructive orphan checkout below: the
      # wrapper needs the real merge ref and its history.
      - id: doc-invariants__guard
        name: doc-guard — added commands/skills update their catalog
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash scripts/ci/check-hooks-on-pr-range.sh -- scripts/hooks/check-doc-guard.sh --pre-push
      # Guard the guard: proves the three gates below catch a stale AGENTS.md,
      # an orphaned debrand rule, and a re-introduced lane-inventory token —
      # and that they do NOT without the staging step.
      #
      # MUST run BEFORE the staging step. It clones this checkout, and the
      # staging step leaves HEAD on an unborn branch — cloning a repo whose HEAD
      # is unborn yields "you appear to have cloned an empty repository" and an
      # EMPTY worktree, so the test would validate nothing and die on setup.
      - id: doc-invariants__self
        name: The doc-invariants job itself is not a no-op
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash scripts/hooks/test-ci-doc-invariants.sh
      # HIMMEL-2037 — the pre-commit `skill-description-cap` hook only sees
      # STAGED files, so it cannot catch an over-cap description that arrived
      # via a bypassed hook. This step re-runs the same lint over the whole
      # tracked set. It takes paths directly, so it needs no staging step and
      # must stay ABOVE the destructive orphan checkout below.
      # -z / xargs -0, not $(…): a tracked path containing whitespace would be
      # word-split by command substitution and the lint would read nonexistent
      # fragments instead of the real file.
      - id: doc-invariants__desc-cap
        name: Skill/command descriptions stay within the 120-char cap
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: git ls-files -z '.claude/commands/*.md' '.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md' '.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md' 'marketplace/plugins/*/commands/*.md' 'marketplace/plugins/*/skills/*/SKILL.md' | xargs -0 node scripts/lanes/skill-cost.mjs --max-desc 120
      # HIMMEL-2051 — same rationale as the description-cap step above: the
      # pre-commit `command-positional-args` hook only sees staged files, so
      # this re-runs the same lint over the whole tracked set.
      # claude-hud is excluded: it is pinned byte-for-byte (HIMMEL-718) and
      # gated by its own drift guard below, not this lint.
      - id: doc-invariants__positional
        name: Commands have no bare $<digit> in their fenced code
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: git ls-files -z '.claude/commands/*.md' 'marketplace/plugins/*/commands/*.md' -- ':!marketplace/plugins/claude-hud' | xargs -0 node scripts/lanes/skill-cost.mjs --check-positional-args
      # HIMMEL-2064 — docs/commands-catalog.md's Description column is
      # generated from `.claude/commands/*.md` frontmatter; this refuses a
      # divergent hand-edit. Reads the tracked files directly, so it needs no
      # staging step and must stay ABOVE the destructive orphan checkout below.
      - id: doc-invariants__catalog
        name: commands-catalog.md Description column matches command frontmatter
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: node scripts/lib/gen-commands-catalog.mjs check
      # HIMMEL-2176 Task 5 — .env.example's generated secrets block is
      # rendered from scripts/himmelctl/lib/secrets-manifest.json; this
      # refuses a divergent hand-edit of either file. Reads the tracked files
      # directly (non-staged check), so it needs no staging step and must
      # stay ABOVE the destructive orphan checkout below, same as the
      # commands-catalog check just above it.
      - id: doc-invariants__secrets-doc
        name: .env.example's generated secrets block matches secrets-manifest.json
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: node scripts/lib/gen-secrets-doc.mjs check
      # HIMMEL-2832/2848 — the v1 adopter docs' executable invariants
      # (budget/forbidden-classes/link-resolution, qualified "profile" +
      # live path/env references) were run by hand only; this wires them into
      # CI. Both checkers read the tracked files directly (no git-diff/staged
      # dependence), so they need no staging step and must stay ABOVE the
      # destructive orphan checkout below, same as the checks just above.
      - id: doc-invariants__llms
        name: v1 adopter docs pass the llms.txt link/budget invariants
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: |
          bash scripts/docs/check-llms-links.sh llms.txt
          bash scripts/docs/check-llms-links.sh docs/setup/install.md
          bash scripts/docs/check-llms-links.sh docs/setup/migrating.md
      - id: doc-invariants__terms
        name: v1 adopter docs pass the qualified-"profile" + live-reference invariants
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: bash scripts/docs/check-doc-terms.sh llms.txt docs/setup/install.md docs/setup/migrating.md
      # HIMMEL-2978 — mirrors the pre-commit marketplace-source-hermetic hook
      # so a PR editing the template is gated even when pre-commit was
      # skipped. Reads the tracked template directly (no git-diff/staged
      # dependence), so it needs no staging step and must stay ABOVE the
      # destructive orphan checkout below, same as the checks just above.
      - id: doc-invariants__hermetic
        name: settings-template marketplace sources stay hermetic
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: bash scripts/check-marketplace-source-hermetic.sh
      # LOAD-BEARING — do not remove (HIMMEL-1305). These gates are pre-commit
      # hooks: each triggers off `git diff --cached` and exits 0 when its inputs
      # are not staged. A CI checkout's index is identical to HEAD, so without
      # this step every gate below no-ops and the job goes green having checked
      # nothing.
      #
      # `checkout --orphan` (NOT `read-tree --empty && add -A`) — the difference
      # is not cosmetic. Re-adding against an unborn HEAD stages the whole tree;
      # re-adding against the REAL HEAD reconstructs an index identical to it, so
      # `git diff --cached` is empty again and nothing fires. That variant appears
      # to work on Windows only because CRLF normalization leaves incidental
      # differences — on this ubuntu runner it stages exactly nothing.
      #
      # This is destructive to the checkout's HEAD, so it goes LAST before the
      # gates and nothing after it may rely on HEAD being a real branch.
      - id: doc-invariants__stage
        name: Stage the committed tree so the gates actually fire
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: git checkout -q --orphan ci-doc-invariants && git add -A
      - id: doc-invariants__agents-md
        name: AGENTS.md is regenerated from CLAUDE.md
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: bash scripts/hooks/check-agents-md-fresh.sh
      - id: doc-invariants__debrand
        name: Every debrand rule still matches CLAUDE.md
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: bash scripts/hooks/check-debrand-coverage.sh
      - id: doc-invariants__lanes
        name: Lane inventory stays out of CLAUDE.md prose
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: bash scripts/hooks/check-lanes-inventory.sh
      # Reached only when the job was not cancelled or timed out; every group
      # output requires it, so a job that stopped early passes no group.
      - id: finished
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: echo "ci-quick ran every group"

  secret-scan:
    # Runs as the secret-scan step group of ci-quick; this job only carries the
    # required context: skipped (green) when the group passed, red otherwise.
    needs: ci-quick
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.ci-quick.outputs.secret-scan != 'pass' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - run: exit 1

  # HIMMEL-3653: HIMMEL-3624 fixed a bracket-expression bug in
  # scripts/lib/unchecked-mktemp.sh that only failed under a real BWK
  # (one-true-awk) — `gawk --posix`/`--lint=fatal` both accept the broken
  # regex (J1288O), so a lint substitute would not catch this class of
  # regression, and Ubuntu PR CI runs everything else under gawk. The only
  # prior BWK coverage was the nightly macOS shell-unit-shard leg (now the
  # os:macos cadence, macos-cadence.yml), which is advisory to main, so a
  # regression here previously reached main unnoticed. This job builds a pinned one-true-awk commit from source
  # (never a branch) and runs the gate's own suite under it, gating every PR.
  bwk-awk-mktemp-gate:
    # Runs as the bwk-awk-mktemp-gate step group of ci-quick; this job only carries the
    # required context: skipped (green) when the group passed, red otherwise.
    needs: ci-quick
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.ci-quick.outputs.bwk-awk-mktemp-gate != 'pass' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - run: exit 1

  # HIMMEL-4301: the unchecked-mktemp gate (scripts/hooks/check-unchecked-mktemp.sh)
  # was pre-commit only (stages: [pre-commit]), so a commit made with the hook
  # skipped or bypassed (UNCHECKED_MKTEMP_OK=1, --no-verify) reached main
  # (#1747, #1771). This re-runs its added-lines scan over the PR's net diff,
  # like plugin-version-bump does for its pre-commit twin. --merge-ref: CI's
  # refs/pull/N/merge has the CURRENT base tip as HEAD^1, so lines main gained
  # since the PR forked are never the PR's. fetch-depth: 0 → HEAD^1 reachable.
  unchecked-mktemp-range:
    # Runs as the unchecked-mktemp-range step group of ci-quick; this job only carries the
    # required context: skipped (green) when the group passed, red otherwise.
    needs: ci-quick
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.ci-quick.outputs.unchecked-mktemp-range != 'pass' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - run: exit 1

  # Commit-time / pre-commit backstop for the 5 leak classes (HIMMEL-2561 /
  # HIMMEL-2705 step 2): catches anything that slipped past the pre-commit
  # hook (a --no-verify commit, a merge, a stale clone). Main and the crons
  # re-scan the whole tracked tree; a PR scans the files it changed
  # (HIMMEL-3898). Public CI has no station-local denylist file, so the
  # hostname class self-skips here (see leak-classes.sh header) — the other
  # 4 classes still run.
  leak-classes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 25 # p95 672s (11m); 2x
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # This is a pull_request workflow, so it checks out and executes
          # contributor code. The default persists the GITHUB_TOKEN into
          # .git/config, where that code can read it.
          persist-credentials: false
          # Depth 2 keeps both parents of the PR merge commit, so HEAD^1 (the
          # current base tip) is reachable for the changed-file list below.
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: leak-classes (PR changed files)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        # Fail closed: a checkout that is not a merge commit, a diff that cannot be
        # computed, or a change to the scanner, its ignore list or this workflow
        # scans the whole tree.
        run: |
          scope=all
          changed="$RUNNER_TEMP/leak-changed.txt"
          touched="$RUNNER_TEMP/leak-touched.txt"
          if git rev-parse -q --verify HEAD^2 > /dev/null && git diff --name-only -z --diff-filter=ACMRT HEAD^1 HEAD > "$changed" && git diff --name-only -z --no-renames HEAD^1 HEAD > "$touched"; then
            scope=files
            # $touched keeps deletions and rename sources, so removing the
            # scanner or its ignore list also scans the whole tree.
            if grep -qzxE '\.github/workflows/ci\.yml|\.leak-classes-ignore|scripts/guardrails/leak-classes\.sh' "$touched"; then
              scope=all
            fi
          fi
          echo "leak-classes scope: $scope"
          if [ "$scope" = files ]; then
            set --
            while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
              if [ -n "$f" ]; then set -- "$@" "$f"; fi
            done < "$changed"
            bash scripts/guardrails/leak-classes.sh --files "$@"
          else
            bash scripts/guardrails/leak-classes.sh --tree
          fi
      - name: leak-classes (whole tree)
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: bash scripts/guardrails/leak-classes.sh --tree

  # Trust-path git subprocess calls must scrub GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/
  # GIT_COMMON_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE before invoking git — an attacker-set value
  # otherwise steers which repo/worktree/index the call answers about
  # (HIMMEL-3570; already caught twice as real bugs, PR 1212 and PR 1217).
  # Main and the crons scan every trust-path file; a PR scans the files it
  # changed (HIMMEL-3898).
  git-env-scrub:
    needs: plan
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_git_env_scrub == 'false') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10 # p95 207s; 2x = 7m, floor 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Depth 2 keeps both parents of the PR merge commit, so HEAD^1 (the
          # current base tip) is reachable for the changed-file list below.
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: git-env-scrub (PR changed files)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        # Fail closed: a checkout that is not a merge commit, a diff that cannot be
        # computed, or a change to the scanner, its baseline, the scrub helpers or
        # this workflow scans every trust-path file.
        run: |
          scope=all
          changed="$RUNNER_TEMP/scrub-changed.txt"
          touched="$RUNNER_TEMP/scrub-touched.txt"
          if git rev-parse -q --verify HEAD^2 > /dev/null && git diff --name-only -z --diff-filter=ACMRT HEAD^1 HEAD > "$changed" && git diff --name-only -z --no-renames HEAD^1 HEAD > "$touched"; then
            scope=files
            # $touched keeps deletions and rename sources, so removing the
            # scanner, its baseline or a scrub helper also scans every trust path.
            if grep -qzxE '\.github/workflows/ci\.yml|scripts/guardrails/check-git-env-scrub\.sh|scripts/guardrails/git-env-baseline\.txt|scripts/lib/git-clean\.sh|scripts/lanes/git-clean\.mjs' "$touched"; then
              scope=all
            fi
          fi
          echo "git-env-scrub scope: $scope"
          if [ "$scope" = files ]; then
