            set --
            while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
              if [ -n "$f" ]; then set -- "$@" "$f"; fi
            done < "$changed"
            bash scripts/guardrails/check-git-env-scrub.sh --files "$@"
          else
            bash scripts/guardrails/check-git-env-scrub.sh --tree
          fi
      - name: git-env-scrub (whole tree)
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: bash scripts/guardrails/check-git-env-scrub.sh --tree

  # Commit-message governance (HIMMEL-594/1483): every non-exempt commit in the
  # PR range must be conventional and ticket-traceable. Reuses the local
  # commit-msg gate (scripts/hooks/check-commit-msg.sh) over the range so CI and
  # the author-time hook agree. fetch-depth: 0 → full history for the range walk.
  commit-lint:
    # Runs as the commit-lint step group of ci-quick; this job only carries the
    # required context: skipped (green) when the group passed, red otherwise.
    needs: ci-quick
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.ci-quick.outputs.commit-lint != 'pass' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - run: exit 1

  # Plugin-version-bump governance (HIMMEL-3551): mirrors the local
  # plugin-version-bump-required pre-commit hook (--bump-required), which only
  # sees STAGED files at commit time, over the whole PR range — so a commit
  # that changes a marketplace/plugins/<p>/ file without bumping that plugin's
  # plugin.json version is caught even when pre-commit was skipped/bypassed.
  # HIMMEL-5177: fetch the current base tip, not the stored event base SHA.
  # Check the PR head, not a merge ref that may include a sibling's bump.
  # Only pull_request runs have a PR's changes to gate.
  plugin-version-bump:
    needs: plan
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_plugin_version_bump == 'false') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10 # p95 9s; floor 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - name: Every plugin file changed in the PR range bumped its version
        env:
          BASE_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
        run: |
          git fetch --no-tags origin "+refs/heads/$BASE_BRANCH:refs/remotes/origin/plugin-bump-base"
          # HIMMEL-5195: run the base tip's checker, not the PR checkout's. The
          # workflow file comes from the merge ref but the checkout is the PR
          # head, so a PR branched before #2341 still carried the old two-dot
          # checker and went red on a plugin bump that landed after it branched.
          checker="$RUNNER_TEMP/plugin-bump-checker"
          mkdir -p "$checker/scripts/lib"
          git show refs/remotes/origin/plugin-bump-base:scripts/check-plugin-drift.sh > "$checker/scripts/check-plugin-drift.sh"
          git show refs/remotes/origin/plugin-bump-base:scripts/lib/vm-mode.sh > "$checker/scripts/lib/vm-mode.sh"
          bash "$checker/scripts/check-plugin-drift.sh" --bump-required refs/remotes/origin/plugin-bump-base

  lint:
    # Ungated (trust judge j2543g): main's --all-files shellcheck sweep reaches
    # executable files (scripts/eval/.../*.sh.ref) no gate line can enumerate, so it
    # runs on every PR like main.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Runs in the prebuilt CI image (docs/internals/ci-image.md). A fork or
    # dependabot[bot] run cannot pull the private package, so it gets '' (no
    # container) and the setup steps gated on !job.container.id install the
    # same tools on the host.
    container:
      image: ${{ !(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository || github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]') && (vars.CI_IMAGE || 'ghcr.io/yotamleo-org/himmel-ci@sha256:6c7a604e4c615486e62303d70039361775a44b1ca3c04eb098a7b06cbbd85009') || '' }} # env-literal-ok: the CI image's own GHCR path, pinned by digest
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ github.token }}
      options: --init --user 1001
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    timeout-minutes: 25 # p95 736s (12m); 2x
    # The image sets no locale (POSIX counts bytes); C.UTF-8 is the host runner's.
    env:
      LANG: C.UTF-8
      LC_ALL: C.UTF-8
    # A container's default run shell is sh; this is the host runner's default.
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash -e {0}
    steps:
      # fetch-depth: 0 so the PR base sha is reachable for the shellcheck range.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      # HIMMEL-4332: flag-registry-lint ran on the runner's unpinned default node.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        if: ${{ !job.container.id }}
        with:
          node-version: '22.23.4'
      # HIMMEL-4265: run the SAME pre-commit shellcheck hook the local gate runs
      # (pinned shellcheck-py version, default severity, .shellcheckrc, and the
      # hook's own vendored/fixture excludes), so nothing the hook refuses can
      # reach main. The old `shellcheck --severity=warning` over a hand-kept
      # file list let info-level findings (SC2119) through CI and fail locally.
      - if: ${{ !job.container.id }}
        run: |
          python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: -r .github/ci-image/requirements-ci.txt
      # HIMMEL-4319: the hook is require_serial, so `--all-files` is one
      # ~9 min CPU-bound shellcheck over ~1460 files. It cannot be sharded:
      # shellcheck resolves `source` across the files of ONE invocation, so
      # SC2034 verdicts depend on the input set (a 100-file shard went red on
      # scripts/lib/check-ci-watch.sh while the serial run was green). So a PR
      # lints the changed files plus their source-graph neighbours in one
      # serial run (all files when in doubt, see the script), and main keeps
      # the full serial sweep as the backstop.
      - name: shellcheck (PR range)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        # The narrowing decision comes from the BASE copy of the script, never the
        # PR's own edited one (a PR could otherwise weaken the check that gates it).
        # Absent or unreadable at base -> the full sweep, never the head copy.
        run: |
          base="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          if git show "$base:scripts/ci/shellcheck-pr-range.sh" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/shellcheck-pr-range.sh" && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/shellcheck-pr-range.sh" ]; then
            bash "$RUNNER_TEMP/shellcheck-pr-range.sh" "$base"
          else
            echo "shellcheck-pr-range: script absent at base, ALL FILES" >&2
            pre-commit run shellcheck --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
          fi
      - name: shellcheck (all files)
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: pre-commit run shellcheck --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
      # HIMMEL-4254 P2: a bypass flag a hook reads but the config UI's display
      # registry lacks is a flag the UI silently cannot show.
      - run: node scripts/install/flag-registry-lint.mjs
      # The history-comment gate also runs as a pre-commit hook, which a session
      # without hooks installed never hits. Run it on the PR range, from the BASE
      # copy (a PR cannot weaken the gate that judges it); a missing base sha or
      # base copy is a red job, never a silent pass.
      - name: history-comment gate (PR range)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$BASE_SHA" ]; then
            echo "history-comment gate: PR base sha missing, cannot evaluate" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          gate="$RUNNER_TEMP/check-history-comments.sh"
          if ! git show "$BASE_SHA:scripts/lint/check-history-comments.sh" > "$gate" || [ ! -s "$gate" ]; then
            echo "history-comment gate: script absent at base $BASE_SHA, cannot evaluate" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          bash "$gate" --range "$BASE_SHA"
      # The hardcoded-env-values lint, same two shapes: the PR range from the BASE
      # copy of the script and its allowlist (a PR cannot widen the allowlist that
      # judges it), then the whole tree at the tip from this checkout on every
      # event. A missing base sha or base copy is a red job, never a silent pass.
      - name: hardcoded-env-values lint (PR range)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$BASE_SHA" ]; then
            echo "hardcoded-env-values lint: PR base sha missing, cannot evaluate" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          gate="$RUNNER_TEMP/base-env-lint/scripts/ci"
          mkdir -p "$gate"
          for f in check-hardcoded-env-values.sh hardcoded-env-values-allow.txt; do
            if ! git show "$BASE_SHA:scripts/ci/$f" > "$gate/$f" || [ ! -s "$gate/$f" ]; then
              echo "hardcoded-env-values lint: $f absent at base $BASE_SHA, cannot evaluate" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          bash "$gate/check-hardcoded-env-values.sh" "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: hardcoded-env-values lint (whole tree)
        run: bash scripts/ci/check-hardcoded-env-values.sh --tree
      # The whole-tree pre-commit gates with no other CI copy, in ONE step (not a
      # job per hook): a session without hooks, or a --no-verify commit, never ran
      # them. Each runs from its BASE copy so a PR cannot weaken the gate that
      # judges it (as do the himmelctl lib and hook launcher it imports); a missing
      # base sha or base copy is a red job, never a silent pass.
      - name: tree-only pre-commit gates (PR range)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          if [ -z "$BASE_SHA" ] || ! git cat-file -e "$BASE_SHA^{commit}"; then
            echo "tree-only gates: PR base sha missing or unreachable, cannot evaluate" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          gates="$RUNNER_TEMP/base-gates"
          for p in scripts/lint/check-mcp-sdk-v1.sh scripts/hooks/check-pip-hashes.sh scripts/install/bundle-registry-lint.mjs; do
            mkdir -p "$gates/$(dirname "$p")"
            if ! git show "$BASE_SHA:$p" > "$gates/$p" || [ ! -s "$gates/$p" ]; then
              echo "tree-only gates: $p absent at base $BASE_SHA, cannot evaluate" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          # the bundle gate imports the himmelctl lib and the hook launcher: stage them from base too
          if ! git archive "$BASE_SHA" scripts/himmelctl scripts/hooks/run-hook-with-bash.js scripts/hooks/hook-integrity.js -o "$gates/deps.tar" || ! tar -xf "$gates/deps.tar" -C "$gates"; then
            echo "tree-only gates: himmelctl lib absent at base $BASE_SHA, cannot evaluate" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          # fail-open-lint cds to its repo root and runs the suite from there: judge the
          # PR tree with the BASE suite, lint and its fixtures laid over a copy of it
          # (the other guardrails files stay the PR's: the lint scans them)
          fo="$(mktemp -d "$RUNNER_TEMP/fail-open-tree.XXXXXX")" || exit 1
          # tracked files via tar, not git archive: a PR-added export-ignore attribute must not hide a file
          # each stage writes a file rather than piping: no producer's failure can hide behind the last command
          if ! git ls-files -z > "$fo.list" || ! tar --null --verbatim-files-from -T "$fo.list" -cf "$fo.pr.tar" || ! tar -xf "$fo.pr.tar" -C "$fo" \
            || ! git archive "$BASE_SHA" scripts/guardrails/lint-fail-open.sh scripts/guardrails/test-lint-fail-open.sh scripts/guardrails/fixtures/fail-open scripts/hooks/check-fail-open-lint.sh -o "$fo.base.tar" || ! tar -xf "$fo.base.tar" -C "$fo"; then
            echo "tree-only gates: fail-open suite absent at base $BASE_SHA, cannot evaluate" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          rc=0
          bash "$gates/scripts/lint/check-mcp-sdk-v1.sh" "$PWD" || rc=1
          (cd "$fo" && bash scripts/hooks/check-fail-open-lint.sh) || rc=1
          node "$gates/scripts/install/bundle-registry-lint.mjs" --root "$PWD" || rc=1
          git ls-files -z -- 'requirements*.txt' '*/requirements*.txt' | xargs -0 -r bash "$gates/scripts/hooks/check-pip-hashes.sh" || rc=1
          exit "$rc"
      # HIMMEL-5526: the skill/command size cap (skill-lint) and the oxlint
      # complexity ratchet + bug-class hardening gates ran only on a committer's
      # machine, so a commit with hooks skipped landed unchecked. A PR runs them
      # on its CHANGED files only; each script exits 0 with "nothing to lint" when
      # none of those files is in its scope, so a docs-only PR passes without
      # fetching oxlint. Every other event (the crons, a dispatch) runs the full
      # tree. Fail closed: a diff that cannot be computed, or a change to a gate,
      # its config or this workflow, runs everything; OXLINT_FAIL_CLOSED=1 turns the
      # gates' own missing-runner fail-open into a red job.
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        if: ${{ !job.container.id }}
        with:
          bun-version-file: .bun-version
      - name: skill size + oxlint complexity/hardening
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          OXLINT_FAIL_CLOSED: '1'
        run: |
          scope=all
          if [ "$EVENT" = pull_request ]; then
            changed="$RUNNER_TEMP/lint-changed.txt"
            if git diff --name-only -z "$BASE_SHA" HEAD > "$changed"; then
              scope=files
              if grep -qzxE '\.github/workflows/ci\.yml|\.pre-commit-config\.yaml|scripts/lint/skill-lint\.sh|scripts/lint/skill-size-allowlist\.txt|scripts/hooks/check-oxlint-(complexity|hardening)\.sh' "$changed"; then
                scope=all
              fi
            fi
          fi
          echo "lint scope: $scope"
          rc=0
          if [ "$scope" = files ]; then
            bash scripts/lint/skill-lint.sh --changed "$BASE_SHA..HEAD" || rc=1
            set --
            while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
              if [ -n "$f" ]; then set -- "$@" "$f"; fi
            done < "$changed"
            bash scripts/hooks/check-oxlint-complexity.sh --files "$@" || rc=1
            bash scripts/hooks/check-oxlint-hardening.sh --files "$@" || rc=1
          else
            bash scripts/lint/skill-lint.sh || rc=1
            bash scripts/hooks/check-oxlint-complexity.sh || rc=1
            bash scripts/hooks/check-oxlint-hardening.sh || rc=1
          fi
          exit "$rc"
      # HIMMEL-6043: shell-lint (mktemp template, GNU flags, errexit leak, POSIX ERE,
      # bash 3.2) ran only on a committer's machine. A PR lints the shell files it
      # CHANGED against the baseline; a diff that cannot be computed fails closed
      # (shell-lint exits 2). The checkout is the PR merge ref, so HEAD^1 is the
      # current base tip; event base.sha can lag it and would lint main's own files.
      # HIMMEL-6315: shell-lint's [shellcheck] check ran the runner's preinstalled 0.9.0 while
      # the pre-commit hook above runs the pinned shellcheck-py, so a PR could pass every local
      # gate and fail here. Install that same rev, read from the pre-commit config, first on PATH.
      - name: pinned shellcheck for shell-lint
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !job.container.id
        run: |
          rev="$(awk '/repo:.*shellcheck-py/ {f=1; next} f && /rev:/ {sub(/^.*rev:[ ]*v?/, ""); print; exit}' .pre-commit-config.yaml)"
          [ -n "$rev" ] || { echo "no shellcheck-py rev in .pre-commit-config.yaml" >&2; exit 1; }
          python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: --target "$RUNNER_TEMP/shellcheck-pinned" -r .github/ci-image/requirements-shellcheck.txt
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/shellcheck-pinned/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          echo "SHELLCHECK_PIN=$rev" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      # The image bakes the same shellcheck-py rev; the next step checks it.
      - name: pinned shellcheck for shell-lint (CI image)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && job.container.id
        run: |
          rev="$(awk '/repo:.*shellcheck-py/ {f=1; next} f && /rev:/ {sub(/^.*rev:[ ]*v?/, ""); print; exit}' .pre-commit-config.yaml)"
          [ -n "$rev" ] || { echo "no shellcheck-py rev in .pre-commit-config.yaml" >&2; exit 1; }
          echo "SHELLCHECK_PIN=$rev" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: shell-lint changed files
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: |
          sc_ver="$(shellcheck --version)"
          echo "$sc_ver"
          printf '%s\n' "$sc_ver" | grep -qxF "version: ${SHELLCHECK_PIN%.*}" || { echo "shellcheck on PATH is not the pinned ${SHELLCHECK_PIN}" >&2; exit 1; }
          bash scripts/lint/shell-lint.sh --changed "HEAD^1..HEAD" --baseline scripts/lint/shell-lint-baseline.tsv
      # HIMMEL-6019: a doc naming a --flag the script it cites lacks; same merge-ref range as above.
      - name: flag-parity changed files
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: bash scripts/lint/flag-parity.sh --changed "HEAD^1..HEAD" --baseline scripts/lint/flag-parity-baseline.tsv

  node-suites:
    needs: plan
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10 # p95 51s (matrix); floor 10
    strategy:
      matrix:
        pkg: [jira, bitbucket, himmel-run, ci-orchestrator]
        # HIMMEL-3813: the two plugin packages live under plugins/, not scripts/.
        # `include` keeps the scripts/* context names (`node-suites (jira)`) that
        # branch protection may require, and adds one per plugin.
        include:
          - pkg: himmel-gh
            dir: plugins/himmel-gh
          - pkg: himmel-jira
            dir: plugins/himmel-jira
          - pkg: himmel-bus
            dir: marketplace/plugins/himmel-bus
            node: '24.22.1'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - if: ${{ !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_node_suites == 'false') }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node || '22.23.4' }}
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: ${{ matrix.dir || format('scripts/{0}', matrix.pkg) }}/package-lock.json
      - if: ${{ !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_node_suites == 'false') }}
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.dir || format('scripts/{0}', matrix.pkg) }}
      - if: ${{ !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_node_suites == 'false') }}
        run: npm test
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.dir || format('scripts/{0}', matrix.pkg) }}

  # HIMMEL-3813: nothing built or ran the jira dist CLI end to end; the unit suite
  # mocks `request`, so a broken tsc build or a dist that crashes at startup merged
  # green. Offline and secret-free (dummy JIRA_* values, a local mock server).
  jira-cli-smoke:
    # Runs as the jira-cli-smoke step group of ci-quick; this job only carries the
    # required context: skipped (green) when the group passed, red otherwise.
    needs: ci-quick
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.ci-quick.outputs.jira-cli-smoke != 'pass' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - run: exit 1

  # HIMMEL-4410 (epic HIMMEL-4409): the credential-free Claude startup suite. A
  # REAL `claude` CLI starts under a fake key inside a loopback-only network
  # namespace and no model turn runs, so it needs no login, no secret and no
  # network (see scripts/testing/fakekey-claude.sh). The CLI is PINNED to an
  # exact version so a Claude Code release cannot redden or silently change this
  # job: to bump it, change CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION below and regenerate
  # .github/claude-cli/package-lock.json on a test VM (the version must exist on npm:
  # `npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code@<v> version`; then in .github/claude-cli:
  # `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts @anthropic-ai/claude-code@<v>`), run
  # `bash scripts/testing/test-fakekey-claude-startup.sh` against that version
  # locally, and fix any assertion the new debug-log wording breaks in the same PR.
  # The suite is SKIP_LISTed in run-shell-tests.sh because the shell-unit shards
  # have no claude CLI; this job is where it runs.
  claude-startup:
    # Runs as the claude-startup step group of ci-quick; this job only carries the
    # required context: skipped (green) when the group passed, red otherwise.
    needs: ci-quick
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.ci-quick.outputs.claude-startup != 'pass' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - run: exit 1

  lanes-and-trust-suites:
    # Ungated (trust judge j2543e): its suites glob-read files no gate group can
    # enumerate, so it runs on every PR like main.
    # HIMMEL-689: scripts/lanes is a zero-dependency ESM test package — no
    # package.json (a committed one under scripts/ trips the npm-audit gates for a
    # package with nothing to install). Run its node:test suites directly.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Runs in the prebuilt CI image (docs/internals/ci-image.md). A fork or
    # dependabot[bot] run cannot pull the private package, so it gets '' (no
    # container) and the setup steps gated on !job.container.id install the
    # same tools on the host.
    container:
      image: ${{ !(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository || github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]') && (vars.CI_IMAGE || 'ghcr.io/yotamleo-org/himmel-ci@sha256:6c7a604e4c615486e62303d70039361775a44b1ca3c04eb098a7b06cbbd85009') || '' }} # env-literal-ok: the CI image's own GHCR path, pinned by digest
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ github.token }}
      options: --init --user 1001
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    timeout-minutes: 15 # p95 423s (7m); 2x
    # The image sets no locale (POSIX counts bytes); C.UTF-8 is the host runner's.
    env:
      LANG: C.UTF-8
      LC_ALL: C.UTF-8
    # A container's default run shell is sh; this is the host runner's default.
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash -e {0}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # HIMMEL-1560: the trust suite's skew regression reads the REAL
          # historical recorder out of git (`git show c49716d5:…`) rather than a
          # synthetic stub, because the thing under test is that an OLD
          # recorder answers `capabilities` with exit 0 and empty stdout. The
          # default checkout is shallow (depth 1), so that object is absent and
          # the test — which ASSERTS the `git show` succeeds rather than
          # silently substituting a stub — would fail here. Full history is the
          # fix; degrading the test to a stub in CI would delete exactly the
          # evidence it exists to provide.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        if: ${{ !job.container.id }}
        with:
          node-version: '22.23.4'
      # HIMMEL-2587: the bench-run-batch dispatch-luna tests shell out to
      # scripts/lanes/bench/bank-snapshot.sh, which runs bun. Without bun the
      # snapshot answers UNKNOWN for both banks and run-batch.sh correctly
      # refuses to start a paid attempt — so those tests abort fail-closed
      # before reaching their assertions and the job stays red. Installing bun
      # keeps the retry-cap / resume / mid-batch-abort contract under a runner
      # check; SKIP-guarding them instead would exit 0 with nothing exercised.
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        if: ${{ !job.container.id }}
        with:
          bun-version-file: .bun-version
      - run: node --test "scripts/lanes/tests/**/*.test.mjs"
      # HIMMEL-1529: same shape — a zero-dependency node:test suite outside any
      # package.json. Listed explicitly because nothing globs for it; an
      # unlisted suite is a suite nobody runs.
      #
      # `ls` first because `node --test` reports zero tests and exits 0 when the
      # glob matches nothing: a renamed or deleted suite would go green with
      # nothing executed. `ls` on an unexpanded pattern fails, so the step does.
      - run: ls scripts/trust/tests/*.test.mjs && node --test "scripts/trust/tests/*.test.mjs"
      # HIMMEL-3827: zero-dependency node:test suites no runner executed. `ls`
      # first for the same vacuous-glob reason as the trust step above.
      - run: ls scripts/where-are-we/tests/*.test.mjs && node --test "scripts/where-are-we/tests/*.test.mjs"
      - run: ls scripts/lessons/tests/*.test.mjs && node --test "scripts/lessons/tests/*.test.mjs"
      # HIMMEL-4501: a glob, not a file list, so a NEW observability .test.mjs
      # runs without a ci.yml edit; `ls` fails on an unexpanded pattern.
      - run: ls scripts/op-env-parity.test.mjs scripts/observability/*.test.mjs && node --test scripts/op-env-parity.test.mjs "scripts/observability/*.test.mjs"
      # HIMMEL-3028: the scripts/hooks + scripts/lib node:test suites
      # (HIMMEL-1578) ran ONLY in the local pre-commit hook until now — that
      # hook deliberately skipped ci.yml because Actions was off on the
      # private repo and the public mirror lacked .claude/settings.json (the
      # wire-hook-bash fixture source). Both premises died 2026-09-09: origin
      # is the public repo with Actions on every PR, and .claude/settings.json
      # is tracked there. Pre-commit stays the fast local gate; this is the
      # authoritative check a bypassed or skipped local hook can no longer
      # dodge (HIMMEL-3025 is exactly the kind of leak this surfaces).
      - run: bash scripts/hooks/check-hook-lib-suites.sh

  guardrail-matrices:
    # Runs as the guardrail-matrices step group of ci-quick; this job only carries the
    # required context: skipped (green) when the group passed, red otherwise.
    needs: ci-quick
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.ci-quick.outputs.guardrail-matrices != 'pass' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - run: exit 1

  # Single-entry os matrix, not a bare job (HIMMEL-1109): the matrix is what
  # names the required check-run context `bun-suites (ubuntu-latest)`. This
  # suite spawns the luna-vitals CLI and connectors/pull-cadence.sh as
  # subprocesses, so its result depends on the host. Windows is dropped
  # (HIMMEL-5729) and macOS is left out: GitHub bills those runners 10x.
  #
  # `shell: bash` because the run lines below chain with `&&`.
  bun-suites:
    # Ungated (trust judge j2543g): `bun test scripts/telegram` globs suites that
    # run extensionless scripts (scripts/claude-codex), so it runs on every PR like main.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    # matrix.os keeps per-PR/per-ref runs from queuing on each other (each PR
    # branch gets its own group, via github.ref).
    concurrency:
      group: bun-suites-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    strategy:
      # HIMMEL-5036: a PR stops at its first red leg.
      fail-fast: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # Runs in the prebuilt CI image (docs/internals/ci-image.md). A fork or
    # dependabot[bot] run cannot pull the private package, so it gets '' (no
    # container) and the setup steps gated on !job.container.id install the
    # same tools on the host.
    container:
      image: ${{ !(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository || github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]') && (vars.CI_IMAGE || 'ghcr.io/yotamleo-org/himmel-ci@sha256:6c7a604e4c615486e62303d70039361775a44b1ca3c04eb098a7b06cbbd85009') || '' }} # env-literal-ok: the CI image's own GHCR path, pinned by digest
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ github.token }}
      options: --init --user 1001
    timeout-minutes: 15 # p95 269s (4.5m); 2x = 9m, kept 15
    # The image sets no locale (POSIX counts bytes); C.UTF-8 is the host runner's.
    env:
      LANG: C.UTF-8
      LC_ALL: C.UTF-8
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      # HIMMEL-4350: this job holds issues:write; the issue steps use gh with
      # GH_TOKEN env and never git, so the persisted checkout token is not needed.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        if: ${{ !job.container.id }}
        with:
          bun-version-file: .bun-version
      - run: cd scripts/luna-vitals && bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts && bash ../ci/run-bun-tests.sh scripts/luna-vitals
      # Must run from the repo root, not scripts/telegram/ — these suites pin
      # their fixtures repo-root-relative, so running them from their own
      # directory fails every wired case (docs/internals/environment-gotchas.md,
      # "The bun test cwd is per-suite"). No `bun install` needed: scripts/telegram
      # has no package.json of its own and the suites run against the repo tree.
      # This is the largest bun test surface in the repo (971 tests) and had no
      # CI step at all until HIMMEL-2620. It runs on both matrix legs because
      # three of its cases are platform-sensitive by construction.
      - run: bash scripts/ci/run-bun-tests.sh scripts/telegram scripts/telegram --dots
      # HIMMEL-3215: the luna source-identity suites (source-identity +
      # backfill, 40 tests) had no CI step, so a regression in
      # scripts/vault/** could merge green. Runs from the repo root like the
      # telegram suite (fixtures are repo-relative). Hermetic: a stub `gh` and a
      # preloaded fetch stub, no network, no live vault. Ubuntu only — the
      # backfill suite prepends a bash `gh` stub to PATH with a `:` separator
      # and calls execFileSync("gh"), which windows-latest cannot resolve, so
      # A step in this job (not a new job) rides the already-required
      # `bun-suites (ubuntu-latest)` context: no branch-protection change.
      - name: Vault tests (ubuntu only)
        if: ${{ matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' }}
        run: bash scripts/ci/run-bun-tests.sh scripts/vault/tests scripts/vault/tests --dots
      # HIMMEL-4254 P3: the read-only config UI (auth/Host/redaction, idle exit,
      # render, the real `himmelctl ui` verb). Repo-root cwd like the suites
      # above; hermetic (stub feed via CONFIG_UI_HIMMELCTL, loopback only).
      # Ubuntu only: it spawns node/bun children with POSIX signal semantics.
      - name: Config UI tests (ubuntu only)
        if: ${{ matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' }}
        run: bash scripts/ci/run-bun-tests.sh scripts/config-ui scripts/config-ui --dots
      # --frozen-lockfile fails if bun.lock has drifted from package.json. Catches
      # the class of bug where a dep range is bumped in package.json but the
      # lockfile is never regenerated (HIMMEL-553). HIMMEL-2620 wired the test
      # run for the suite that was always there under tests/.
      - run: cd marketplace/plugins/luna-correlate && bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts && bash ../../../scripts/ci/run-bun-tests.sh marketplace/plugins/luna-correlate
      # HIMMEL-3813: telegram-himmel's own suite (tests/poller-gate-shape.test.ts)
      # had no CI step. Ubuntu only, like the vault step: its fixtures are
      # POSIX-shaped and a red non-gating Windows leg would file a spurious issue.
      - name: telegram-himmel plugin tests (ubuntu only)
        if: ${{ matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' }}
        run: cd marketplace/plugins/telegram-himmel && bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts && bash ../../../scripts/ci/run-bun-tests.sh marketplace/plugins/telegram-himmel
      # HIMMEL-3827: fleet-control (9 files) and observability (bun files) had
      # no CI step. Repo-root cwd like the suites above; ubuntu only (POSIX
      # fixtures, spawned servers) so the non-gating Windows leg stays quiet.
      - name: fleet-control + observability tests (ubuntu only)
        if: ${{ matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' }}
        run: ls scripts/fleet-control/tests/*.test.ts scripts/observability/*.test.ts && bash scripts/ci/run-bun-tests.sh scripts/fleet-control+observability scripts/fleet-control scripts/observability --path-ignore-patterns='scripts/observability/*.test.mjs' --dots
      - name: Upload bun flake ledger
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: bun-suite-flakes-${{ matrix.os }}-attempt${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ~/.himmel/suite-flake-ledger.jsonl
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 30

  # CLAUDE.md-derived content invariants (HIMMEL-1305). The local pre-commit
  # copies of these gates judge the STAGED source, but they execute the repo's
  # own tooling — scripts/agents-md/generate.mjs, scripts/guardrails/lib.sh, and
  # the gate scripts themselves — from the WORKING TREE. An unstaged edit to
  # that tooling can therefore approve a commit the edit is not part of.
  # himmel accepts working-tree execution as the local convention (rationale:
  # docs/internals/enforcement.md § Gates execute working-tree tooling); this
  # job is the backstop. A CI checkout has no working tree to diverge from, so
  # running the SAME gate scripts here validates committed source with committed
  # tooling by construction.
  #
  # WHERE THIS RUNS: Actions is disabled on the private repo by design (the
  # split is pre-commit locally, Actions on the public mirror), so this job
  # gates the PUBLIC tree after propagation — not the private PR. That is still
  # worth having: propagation is a re-projection, an independent diff surface
  # where a CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/debrand inconsistency would land unchecked.
  # Do not read a green private PR as evidence these gates ran.
  #
  # These gates are himmel-dev-only — they no-op without the gitignored
  # `.himmel-dev` marker, which keeps them off for adopters running himmel as a
  # harness. CI is a contributor context, so create the marker first, otherwise
  # every step below silently passes without checking anything.
  doc-invariants:
    # Runs as the doc-invariants step group of ci-quick; this job only carries the
    # required context: skipped (green) when the group passed, red otherwise.
    needs: ci-quick
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.ci-quick.outputs.doc-invariants != 'pass' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - run: exit 1

  # Security / dependency scanning lane (HIMMEL-510): mirrors the local
  # pre-commit/pre-push security gates (.pre-commit-config.yaml) by invoking the
  # SAME scripts/hooks/* gate scripts, so CI and the author-time hooks stay in
  # lockstep — a vuln/license/lockfile/secret problem that blocks a local push
  # also blocks the PR. Secret-free + ubuntu-only; the only network reached is
  # public (GitHub releases for the gitleaks binary, the npm registry for audit/
  # license/signature checks). Deferred to a follow-up: bandit (python SAST —
  # needs a baseline #nosec triage of pre-existing VM/SSH tooling before it can
  # gate green) and better-npm-audit (redundant with the npm-audit gate below).
  security-scan:
    needs: plan
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Runs in the prebuilt CI image (docs/internals/ci-image.md). A fork or
    # dependabot[bot] run cannot pull the private package, so it gets '' (no
    # container) and the setup steps gated on !job.container.id install the
    # same tools on the host.
    container:
      image: ${{ !(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository || github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]') && (vars.CI_IMAGE || 'ghcr.io/yotamleo-org/himmel-ci@sha256:6c7a604e4c615486e62303d70039361775a44b1ca3c04eb098a7b06cbbd85009') || '' }} # env-literal-ok: the CI image's own GHCR path, pinned by digest
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ github.token }}
      options: --init --user 1001
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    # This job does the most network I/O in the workflow (gitleaks download +
    # `npm ci` across ~9 packages); cap it so a hung download/install can't
    # burn a full 6h runner slot (codex-3 CR hardening).
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # The image sets no locale (POSIX counts bytes); C.UTF-8 is the host runner's.
    env:
      LANG: C.UTF-8
      LC_ALL: C.UTF-8
    # A container's default run shell is sh; this is the host runner's default.
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash -e {0}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - if: ${{ !job.container.id && !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_deps_audit == 'false') }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22.23.4'
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: '**/package-lock.json'
      - if: ${{ !job.container.id && !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_deps_audit == 'false') }}
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version-file: .bun-version

      # gitleaks: pinned to the SAME version as the pre-commit hook
      # (.pre-commit-config.yaml → gitleaks rev v8.30.1) and reuses .gitleaks.toml,
      # so a secret the local hook catches is caught here too. `dir` scans the
      # checked-out working tree; gitleaks exits non-zero when a leak is found.
      - name: gitleaks secret scan (reuses .gitleaks.toml)
        if: ${{ !job.container.id }}
        run: |
          ver=8.30.1
          # Pin the exact release bytes: verify the published SHA256 before
          # extracting/executing, so a tampered or MITM'd download cannot run
          # (it would be silly for the SECURITY lane to run an unverified
          # scanner binary). Update `sha` in lockstep with `ver`.
          sha=551f6fc83ea457d62a0d98237cbad105af8d557003051f41f3e7ca7b3f2470eb
          curl -sSfL "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${ver}/gitleaks_${ver}_linux_x64.tar.gz" -o /tmp/gitleaks.tgz
          echo "${sha}  /tmp/gitleaks.tgz" | sha256sum -c -
          tar -xzf /tmp/gitleaks.tgz -C /tmp gitleaks
          /tmp/gitleaks dir . --config .gitleaks.toml --redact --no-banner
      # The image bakes the same pinned, sha-verified release (test-ci-image.sh).
      - name: gitleaks secret scan (CI image)
        if: ${{ job.container.id }}
        run: |
          gitleaks version
          gitleaks dir . --config .gitleaks.toml --redact --no-banner

      # Lockfile integrity (npm + bun) — pre-commit `lockfile-integrity`.
      # npm path is `npm ci --dry-run` (no install needed); bun path is
      # `bun install --frozen-lockfile --dry-run` (setup-bun above provides bun).
      - name: lockfile integrity (npm + bun)
        if: ${{ !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_deps_audit == 'false') }}
        run: bash scripts/hooks/check-lockfile-integrity.sh

      # uv lock integrity (python) — pre-commit `uv-lock-integrity`. No
      # pyproject.toml in the tree today, so this self-skips (kept for lockstep:
      # the day a python project lands, CI gates its uv.lock with no further edit).
      - name: uv lock integrity (python)
        if: ${{ !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_deps_audit == 'false') }}
        run: bash scripts/hooks/check-uv-lock.sh

      # npm audit (production, high+) — pre-push `npm-audit`. Self-installs prod
      # deps (`npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts`) for every committed
      # package.json, leaving node_modules in place for the signatures step below.
      - name: npm audit (production, high+)
        if: ${{ !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_deps_audit == 'false') }}
        run: bash scripts/hooks/check-npm-audit.sh

      # npm license allowlist — pre-push `npm-licenses`.
      - name: npm license allowlist
        if: ${{ !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_deps_audit == 'false') }}
        run: bash scripts/hooks/check-npm-licenses.sh

      # HIMMEL-2573: this gate has a hard floor (npm >= 11) that the pinned
      # node-version above does not meet — node 22 bundles npm 10.9.8. That
      # floor and this job's runtime can drift apart silently: the only
      # symptom was an error that read like a package problem, and it went
      # unnoticed because it passes on every developer machine (newer npm
      # installed locally) and this repo never ran the workflow before
      # (Actions is off on the private repo by design). Upgrade npm here
      # rather than bumping node-version — node 22 is the tested runtime for
      # the whole workflow and a signature gate shouldn't quietly change that.
      # Print the version so the next time this floor and this runtime drift
      # apart, it's one glance at the log instead of an investigation.
      - name: upgrade npm to meet the audit-signatures floor (>= 11)
        if: ${{ !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_deps_audit == 'false') }}
        env:
          IN_IMAGE: ${{ job.container.id }}
        run: |
          ${IN_IMAGE:+sudo} npm i -g npm@^11
          npm --version

      # npm audit signatures (production) — pre-push `npm-audit-signatures`. This
      # gate does NOT self-install; it relies on the node_modules the npm-audit
      # step above materialized for the scripts/{jira,bitbucket,himmel-run}
      # packages, so it MUST run after that step.
      - name: npm audit signatures (production)
        if: ${{ !(needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.run_deps_audit == 'false') }}
        run: bash scripts/hooks/check-npm-audit-signatures.sh

  # Ubuntu only (HIMMEL-5729 dropped the nightly Windows leg). macOS (10x) is
  # NOT here (HIMMEL-3902): it is the os:macos cadence, macos-cadence.yml. A red
  # nightly leg becomes its own split slice — docs/internals/testing.md.
  #
  # This is the working matrix — sharded per OS (HIMMEL-2872) so the ubuntu
  # legs finish in parallel instead of serially. The shard COUNT is spelled in
  # exactly two places, both below and both of which must agree: the `shard:`
  # matrix list and the `--shard …/<n>` run argument. Deliberately not repeated
  # here — a third copy is a third thing to forget. `shell-unit` below is
  # the aggregating gate that rolls this matrix up into the one required
  # check-run context branch protection names.
  shell-unit-shard:
    # HIMMEL-5649: the plan job (pull_request only) lists the shards that have a
    # suite; an empty list skips the whole job, so a docs-only PR starts no shard.
    # Fail-open like every gated job: a plan that failed, was skipped (cron,
    # dispatch) or printed no list starts all 8.
    needs: plan
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.plan.outputs.shards != '[]' }}
    strategy:
      # Every shard runs to the end, a PR's too, so one run reports every red
      # shard; the fail-fast-shell-unit-shard twin still cancels the rest of
      # the run once the matrix has finished red.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest]
        # shard: [1..N] fans run-shell-tests.sh across N runners (HIMMEL-2872).
        # On a pull_request the plan sizes N (at most vars.CI_MAX_SHARDS, 20 unset,
        # HIMMEL-6585; 20 is where a full pr-mode selection's longest shard is its
        # longest suite, HIMMEL-6598);
        # without a plan (push, schedule, dispatch) N stays 8: those runs gate no
        # PR, and a list sized from the variable cannot be written as an expression.
        # The `8` fallbacks here, in the run
        # step's `/N` and in the aggregator's SHARD_TOTAL are spellings of the same
        # number — GitHub Actions has no way to derive one from the other
        # (strategy.job-total counts os×shard, not shard alone), so a change to
        # the no-plan count must edit all of them or the split stops being a
        # partition (the aggregator's manifest check then goes red). The plan's
        # shards and shard_total outputs always travel together, so raising
        # the variable never splits the fallbacks. Went from 6 to 8 because 6 measured an 18m23s
        # slowest shard (3m18s fastest) — round-robin, not the count, dumped
        # the corpus's two heaviest suites onto one shard (719s of its 1065s);
        # replaying measured durations predicts 9.9m at 8 but 10.7m at 12, so
        # more shards isn't monotonically better — a duration-aware split is
        # the real fix (follow-up).
        shard: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.shards || '[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]') }}
    # HIMMEL-5641: a same-repo pull_request opened by an operator account runs on
    # the himmel-vm self-hosted runner while the kill switch (repo variable
    # HIMMEL_VM_RUNNER, set by vm-runner.sh on/off) is 'on'; everything else — a
    # fork PR, any other author, push, schedule, dispatch, the switch off or
    # unset — runs on matrix.os. Never pull_request_target. The accounts mirror
    # scripts/vm/ci-runner/job-started-hook.sh, which refuses the rest anyway, so
    # a job this expression would misroute fails there instead of running code.
    runs-on: ${{ (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository && contains(fromJSON('["yotamleo","yotamleo11-test"]'), github.event.pull_request.user.login) && contains(fromJSON('["yotamleo","yotamleo11-test"]'), github.actor) && contains(fromJSON('["yotamleo","yotamleo11-test"]'), github.triggering_actor) && vars.HIMMEL_VM_RUNNER == 'on') && fromJSON('["self-hosted","himmel-vm"]') || (vars.CI_GCP == 'on' && contains(fromJSON('["yotamleo","yotamleo11-test"]'), github.actor) && contains(fromJSON('["yotamleo","yotamleo11-test"]'), github.triggering_actor) && (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository && contains(fromJSON('["yotamleo","yotamleo11-test"]'), github.event.pull_request.user.login)))) && fromJSON('["self-hosted","gcp"]') || matrix.os }}
    # Runs in the prebuilt CI image (docs/internals/ci-image.md). A fork or
    # dependabot[bot] run cannot pull the private package, so it gets '' (no
    # container) and the setup steps gated on !job.container.id install the
    # same tools on the host.
    # A self-hosted route (himmel-vm, gcp) keeps its own baked tools: '' too.
    # --init: an init as PID 1 reaps orphaned descendants, as on the host.
    # --privileged: bwrap and unshare need user namespaces inside the container.
    container:
      image: ${{ !(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository || github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]' || vars.HIMMEL_VM_RUNNER == 'on' || vars.CI_GCP == 'on') && (vars.CI_IMAGE || 'ghcr.io/yotamleo-org/himmel-ci@sha256:6c7a604e4c615486e62303d70039361775a44b1ca3c04eb098a7b06cbbd85009') || '' }} # env-literal-ok: the CI image's own GHCR path, pinned by digest
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ github.token }}
      options: --init --user 1001 --privileged
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    # HIMMEL-6272: otherwise, while repo variable CI_GCP is 'on' (setting it to
    # 'off' is the instant kill switch), a dispatch or a same-repo
    # pull_request by the same operator accounts runs on an ephemeral GCP spot
    # runner (label gcp, one job per VM, scripts/ci/gcp-runners.sh up). A fork PR,
    # any other author and a schedule never reach it (ci.yml has no push trigger;
    # the 45 min VM cap is under the nightly shards).
    # The VM image carries the tools the github-hosted-gated steps below install.
    # HIMMEL-3919: bound the job (default is 6 h; main-push runs share one
    # non-cancelling concurrency group, so one hung shard queued every later
    # main run). The nightly SUITE_TIER_MODE=all legs are far slower than the
    # fast-tier push/PR runs: ubuntu shard 8 took 35-38 min.
    # suite-durations.tsv is the fast tier only (~18 min slowest
    # shard). 60 is ~1.7x the slowest nightly shard. There are no macos rows in
    # this matrix (macos-cadence.yml / os-verify.yml carry their own 120).
    # HIMMEL-5036: cap NOT lowered. PR shards run only impacted suites (p95 1676s,
    # 28m, over 10 green PR runs); the main sweep runs the full set per shard and
    # the p95 measured here does not cover it, so 60 stays until sweep data does.
    timeout-minutes: 60
    # The image sets no locale (POSIX counts bytes); C.UTF-8 is the host runner's.
    env:
      LANG: C.UTF-8
      LC_ALL: C.UTF-8
    # A container's default run shell is sh; this is the host runner's default.
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash -e {0}
    steps:
      # fetch-depth: 0 (not the default shallow clone) so --changed-since below
      # can resolve a pull_request's base SHA, which a depth-1 checkout of the
      # head ref does not carry.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      # arm-resume's non-dry-run cases exercise the real `at` scheduler backend,
      # which the supported runtime provides (HIMMEL-594 `ubuntu.sh` installs +
      # enables at/atd). GitHub's ubuntu image ships without `at`, so CI fell back
      # to the crontab path and ~2 arm-resume cases diverged from a real install.
      # Install + enable it on Linux so CI mirrors the supported runtime
      # (HIMMEL-619). Scoped to Linux.
      # HIMMEL-2871: the runner image preinstalls third-party apt sources
      # (Google Chrome, Microsoft, Azure CLI) we never use; when one of those
      # goes inconsistent upstream, `apt-get update` exits 100 and this step
      # kills the whole job before any suite runs. Drop those lists first so
      # the update depends only on the Ubuntu archive we actually need.
      # No `.list`/`.sources` suffix on the glob: ubuntu-24.04 runner images
      # ship these as deb822 `.sources` files, not legacy one-line `.list`
      # files, and a suffix-anchored glob silently matched nothing.
      # HIMMEL-4912: install bubblewrap (and socat, which the live pilot-4869
      # jail checks drive) here too so Linux corpus/replay suites exercise the
      # real containment boundary rather than capability-skip.
      # HIMMEL-5641: the apt, sudo and pip steps below run on a GitHub-hosted
      # runner only. The himmel-vm guest's `runner` user has no sudo and carries
      # at/atd, bubblewrap, socat, ffmpeg and pre-commit from guest-provision.sh.
      - name: Record runner image (apt cache key)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && runner.environment == 'github-hosted' && !job.container.id
        run: echo "APT_IMAGE=${ImageVersion:-unknown}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Cache apt debs (at/atd)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && runner.environment == 'github-hosted' && !job.container.id
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/apt-archives
          key: apt-${{ runner.os }}-${{ env.APT_IMAGE }}-at-${{ hashFiles('.github/scripts/apt-install.sh') }}
      - name: Install + enable at/atd (Linux — arm-resume scheduler backend)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && runner.environment == 'github-hosted' && !job.container.id
        # HIMMEL-3919: a hung dpkg/apt lock held this step ~1.5 h. HIMMEL-2872:
        # apt-install.sh bounds every apt call with a `timeout` and a dpkg-lock
        # wait, and tries cached debs, then the runner's mirror, then an
        # alternate mirror (HIMMEL-4073: the plain install comes before any index
        # refresh). Worst case 60 + 120 + 180 + 180 s = 9 min; the step cap is 13.
        timeout-minutes: 13
        run: |
          started=$SECONDS
          trap 'echo "at/atd install: duration_seconds=$((SECONDS - started))"' EXIT
          sudo rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/google-chrome* /etc/apt/sources.list.d/microsoft-* /etc/apt/sources.list.d/azure-cli*
          bash .github/scripts/apt-install.sh at bubblewrap socat
          sudo systemctl enable --now atd || sudo service atd start || echo "atd start failed; checking is-active"  # t13b-ok: stock at daemon on a throwaway CI runner, not a himmel service
          systemctl is-active --quiet atd || { echo "::error::atd is not active after install; the arm-resume scheduler backend would fail later with an unrelated symptom" >&2; exit 1; }
      # The image bakes at; a container has no systemd, so start the daemon here.
      - name: Start atd (CI image)
        if: ${{ job.container.id }}
        timeout-minutes: 1
        run: |
          sudo atd
          pgrep -x atd > /dev/null || { echo "::error::atd is not running in the CI image; the arm-resume scheduler backend would fail later with an unrelated symptom" >&2; exit 1; }
      # HIMMEL-4912: ubuntu-24.04 refuses unprivileged user namespaces by default
      # (AppArmor), so bwrap fails with `RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted` and
      # the sandboxed suites fail or hit their caps. Same step as claude-startup.
      - name: Allow unprivileged user namespaces (Linux — bwrap sandbox)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && runner.environment == 'github-hosted'
        run: sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0 || true
      # HIMMEL-2742: same shape as HIMMEL-2587 (lanes-and-trust-suites) — a
      # suite in this corpus (test-wizard-luna-sections.sh) shells out to bun
      # and fails closed ("required test tool not found before PATH scrub:
      # bun") without it. Installing bun keeps that hermetic PATH-scrub case
      # under a runner check; a self-skip would exit 0 with nothing exercised.
      # The himmel-vm guest must not restore a cache entry a
      # hosted run wrote (it restores, then the bun executable is missing).
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        if: ${{ !job.container.id }}
        with:
          bun-version-file: .bun-version
          no-cache: ${{ runner.environment != 'github-hosted' }}
      # HIMMEL-3193: the run step below now covers marketplace/ (root `.`), where
      # the obsidian-triage suites need js-yaml + playwright from
      # tools/node_modules. ensure-deps.sh installs them and exits non-zero on
      # ANY npm/network failure (no `|| true`, no continue-on-error), so a flaky
      # install fails THIS step loudly instead of surfacing as a dozen
      # unrelated suite reds. Pinned by test-run-shell-tests.sh Case 23f.
      - name: Install obsidian-triage tool deps (marketplace suites)
        run: bash marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/tools/ensure-deps.sh
      # HIMMEL-4802: test-x-media-hls-ffmpeg.sh runs a REAL ffmpeg over the
      # playlists x-media-fetch.py rewrites (every other suite stubs it). It
      # SKIPs without ffmpeg, so this step pins the noble 6.1 build and then
      # sets HIMMEL_REQUIRE_FFMPEG=1, turning that SKIP into a FAIL here. A
      # runner image that drops the 6.1 package fails this step loudly; re-pin
      # deliberately. Linux only: the nightly windows leg keeps the SKIP.
      - name: Record runner image (apt cache key)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && runner.environment == 'github-hosted' && !job.container.id
        run: echo "APT_IMAGE=${ImageVersion:-unknown}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Cache apt debs (ffmpeg)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && runner.environment == 'github-hosted' && !job.container.id
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/apt-archives
          key: apt-${{ runner.os }}-${{ env.APT_IMAGE }}-ffmpeg-${{ hashFiles('.github/scripts/apt-install.sh') }}
      - name: Install pinned ffmpeg (Linux — obsidian-triage HLS suite)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && runner.environment == 'github-hosted' && !job.container.id
        timeout-minutes: 13
        run: |
          bash .github/scripts/apt-install.sh 'ffmpeg=7:6.1.*'
          ffmpeg -version | head -n 1
          echo "HIMMEL_REQUIRE_FFMPEG=1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      # The guest and the CI image bake the same ffmpeg 6.1; the require flag still applies.
      - name: Require the guest's baked ffmpeg (self-hosted himmel-vm)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && (runner.environment != 'github-hosted' || job.container.id)
        run: |
          ffmpeg -version | head -n 1
          echo "HIMMEL_REQUIRE_FFMPEG=1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      # HIMMEL-5120(b): scripts/guardrails/test-gitleaks-retired-org.sh SKIPs
      # without gitleaks on PATH, and the pinned binary was only downloaded to
      # /tmp inside secret-scan. Put the SAME pinned, sha-verified release on
      # PATH for every ubuntu shard: the bin-pack (duration ledger) decides
      # which shard holds the suite, so any single-shard pin could go stale.
      # ponytail: ~8 MB download x8 shards, upgrade by pinning to the shard
      # the ledger assigns once run-shell-tests.sh can print it (HIMMEL-5120).
      # Keep ver/sha in lockstep with secret-scan.
      - name: Put pinned gitleaks on PATH (Linux — retired-org suite)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && !job.container.id
        run: |
          ver=8.30.1
          sha=551f6fc83ea457d62a0d98237cbad105af8d557003051f41f3e7ca7b3f2470eb
          curl -sSfL "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${ver}/gitleaks_${ver}_linux_x64.tar.gz" -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks.tgz"
          echo "${sha}  $RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks.tgz" | sha256sum -c -
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks-bin"
          tar -xzf "$RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks.tgz" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks-bin" gitleaks
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks-bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      # HIMMEL-6548: scripts/lib/test-bash-ast.sh SKIPs its model rows without
      # shfmt, and the guards migrated onto bash-ast.sh deny without it. Put the
      # SAME pinned, sha-verified release the CI image carries
      # (.github/ci-image/Dockerfile) on PATH for every ubuntu shard, and set
      # HIMMEL_REQUIRE_SHFMT=1 so a missing binary fails the suite, not skips it.
      # Keep ver/sha in lockstep with the Dockerfile.
      - name: Put pinned shfmt on PATH (Linux — bash-ast model rows)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          ver=3.14.1
          sha=76e77641faa025814b77f153b29796b8e6fa2fca03e0c76a691608b86c7ea7bf
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/shfmt-bin"
          curl -sSfL "https://github.com/mvdan/sh/releases/download/v${ver}/shfmt_v${ver}_linux_amd64" -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/shfmt-bin/shfmt"
          echo "${sha}  $RUNNER_TEMP/shfmt-bin/shfmt" | sha256sum -c -
          chmod 755 "$RUNNER_TEMP/shfmt-bin/shfmt"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/shfmt-bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          echo "HIMMEL_REQUIRE_SHFMT=1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      # HIMMEL-2223 codex-3: scripts/test-template-nostash-hooks.sh hard-SKIPs
      # (exit 0) without pre-commit on PATH — the exact vacuous-SKIP shape
      # called out for the Windows vault suites above (LUNA-131) — so without
      # this install the suite is a permanent no-op here, never exercising the
      # real fixer hooks. `shell: bash` matches the Windows install pattern
      # above: python -m pip works identically on every OS in this matrix.
      - name: Install pre-commit (scripts/test-template-nostash-hooks.sh)
        if: runner.environment == 'github-hosted' && !job.container.id
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: -r .github/ci-image/requirements-ci.txt
      # Explicit `bash` prefix: on windows-latest the default run shell is pwsh,
      # but Git Bash is preinstalled + on PATH, so `bash …` runs under MSYS2.
      # FAIL_LOG_DIR: full failed-suite logs land there and upload as an
      # artifact below — the inline tail is bounded, so without this the
      # failing assertion can be unrecoverable from Actions logs (HIMMEL-963).
      # SUITE_TIER_MODE (HIMMEL-2166 / HIMMEL-6598): pr on a pull_request (the
      # suite-tiers.tsv floor plus the impacted suites), all on every other run
      # (the nightly, the main-sweep cron, a workflow_dispatch). Rollback is this
      # 'pr' back to 'fast' here, in the aggregator and in the plan step.
      # The aggregator below carries the same expression.
      # SUITE_CHANGED_SINCE: only on pull_request, where a base SHA exists —
      # a docs-only PR then skips the whole corpus (run-shell-tests.sh's own
      # docs-only fast lane); push/schedule/dispatch have no PR base to diff.
      # Scan root `.` (HIMMEL-3193) = scripts/ + templates/ + marketplace/; the
      # duration ledger keys all three, so the bin-pack balances across them.
      # SUITE_IMPACTED_FROM_BASE (HIMMEL-3897): on a pull_request to the default
      # branch, the shards run only the suites the BASE commit's
      # scripts/ci/impacted-selection.sh selects for the PR diff — or the full
      # sweep, which it decides for any trust-path change (this file,
      # run-shell-tests.sh, the selector, the trust list), a base that is not on
      # main (spec hole H1), or any doubt. A PR to another branch, schedule
      # and dispatch pass '' = the full sweep. The 8 shards stay 8 required
      # contexts either way; a docs-only PR's shards exit 0 with nothing to run.
      # SUITE_MANIFEST: the selection this shard acted on and every suite's fate,
      # uploaded below and verified by the shell-unit aggregator.
      # HIMMEL-6037 / HIMMEL-6621: the shard runs through home-canary.sh, so HOME
      # and USERPROFILE point at a sandbox holding a honeytoken .env and the shard
      # fails when the token reaches the output or the file is read (the PR 2883
      # shape). The shard has the tools, so a suite failure is a shard failure
      # (the runner's exit is not downgraded). The bound sits under the job cap of 60.
      - run: bash scripts/ci/home-canary.sh --shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ needs.plan.outputs.shard_total || 8 }} .
        env:
          HOME_CANARY_REQUIRE_ATIME: "1"
          HOME_CANARY_TIMEOUT: "3300"
          FAIL_LOG_DIR: failed-suite-logs
          SUITE_TIER_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'pr' || 'all' }}
          SUITE_STOP_ON_FAIL: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && '1' || '' }}
          # HIMMEL-4912: the shards (60 min) always run the fast guard-corpus
          # subset; the full replay runs in the schedule-only guard-corpus-full job.
          GUARD_CORPUS_TIER: fast
          SUITE_CHANGED_SINCE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.base.sha || '' }}
          SUITE_IMPACTED_FROM_BASE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.base.ref == github.event.repository.default_branch && github.event.pull_request.base.sha || '' }}
          SUITE_MANIFEST: shard-manifest/manifest-shard${{ matrix.shard }}.txt
      - name: Upload shard manifest
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: shell-unit-manifest-${{ matrix.os }}-shard${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: shard-manifest/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 14
          # A re-run shard replaces its manifest, so the aggregator reads the
          # latest attempt's.
          overwrite: true
      - name: Upload shell flake ledger
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: shell-suite-flakes-${{ matrix.os }}-shard${{ matrix.shard }}-attempt${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: failed-suite-logs/flake-ledger.jsonl
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 30
      - name: Upload failed-suite logs
        if: failure() || cancelled()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: shell-unit-failed-logs-${{ matrix.os }}-shard${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: failed-suite-logs/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 14

  # Aggregating gate (HIMMEL-2872). Four things worth knowing before touching
  # this job:
  #
  # 1. The single-value `os` matrix below is deliberate and load-bearing: it
  #    is what makes the check-run context `shell-unit (ubuntu-latest)` rather
  #    than a bare `shell-unit`, keeping the required branch-protection
  #    context byte-for-byte identical to what it was before the work above
  #    was sharded. Sharding the work must not rename the gate.
  # 2. `needs.shell-unit-shard.result` is the matrix ROLLUP, `success` only
  #    when every leg that CAN fail the matrix succeeded. A job-level
  #    `continue-on-error` failure is NOT counted against that rollup — this
  #    job never has to name any OS itself.
  # 3. `if: always()` plus the explicit `!= success` test below is the
  #    fail-CLOSED shape: `failure`, `cancelled` AND `skipped` all redden this
  #    job. A bare `needs:` without `always()` would SKIP this job whenever a
  #    shard failed — and a required check that never reports leaves the PR
  #    hanging rather than red.
  # 4. No setup: this job is a verdict, not work. It DOES check out (HIMMEL-3166)
  #    — the report steps below run a repo script, and without a checkout
  #    `bash scripts/ci/shell-extended-nightly-issue.sh` died with rc=127 on
  #    the 2026-09-18 nightly, so the alert never fired. A plain checkout
  #    rather than a sparse `scripts/ci` one: the script sources nothing today,
  #    but this leg only runs unwatched, so a future `source` of a sibling lib
  #    would re-break it silently.
  #
  # 5. issues:write (beyond the workflow-level contents:read) is needed only
  #    by the shell-extended-nightly-issue.sh steps below — scoped to this
  #    job alone.
  #    HIMMEL-3132: SUITE_TIER_DEFAULT `extended` suites only run under
  #    SUITE_TIER_MODE=all (the schedule leg, set above at
  #    shell-unit-shard), so a red extended suite only ever reddens THIS
  #    job on that leg — a run nobody watches interactively. Without these
  #    steps that failure is silent even though the job itself goes red.
  shell-unit:
    needs: [shell-unit-shard, plan]
    if: always()
    # HIMMEL-3788: a manual dispatch on an arbitrary branch/PR head must not
    # post a check-run literally named "shell-unit (ubuntu-latest)" --
    # identical to (and newer than) the PR's own required check -- or GitHub's
    # required-check evaluation and check-ci.sh both read the dispatch run's
    # result and shadow the PR's. HIMMEL-3853 removed the all-OS dispatch input,
    # so a dispatch is now ubuntu-only; the distinct name is kept as the
    # name-collision guard.
    # schedule/pull_request keep the unchanged name.
    name: shell-unit${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && ' (dispatch verify)' || '' }} (${{ matrix.os }})
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
      actions: read
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 10 # p95 179s; 2x = 6m, floor 10
    steps:
      # Full history: impacted-selection.sh diffs base...HEAD and checks the
      # base is on origin/main, exactly as the shards did.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Every gating shell-unit shard must have passed
        env:
          SHARDS_RESULT: ${{ needs.shell-unit-shard.result }}
          PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }}
          PLAN_SHARDS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.shards }}
        run: |
          echo "shell-unit-shard matrix rollup: $SHARDS_RESULT"
          # HIMMEL-5649: no shard has a suite -> the shard job was skipped by its
          # `if`. That is a pass ONLY when the plan itself succeeded and said so;
          # the accounting step below still proves nothing was selected.
          if [ "$SHARDS_RESULT" = "skipped" ] && [ "$PLAN_RESULT" = "success" ] && [ "$PLAN_SHARDS" = "[]" ]; then
            SHARDS_RESULT=success
          fi
          if [ "$SHARDS_RESULT" != "success" ]; then
            echo "::error::shell-unit shards did not all pass (matrix rollup: $SHARDS_RESULT) — see the shell-unit-shard jobs on this run."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: every gating shell-unit shard passed."
      - name: Download shard manifests
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        # HIMMEL-5649: a PR whose shards all had no work uploads no manifest. A
        # failed download is not forgiven: every shard not named in --absent-ok
        # below must still have its manifest, so the verify step goes red.
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: shell-unit-manifest-ubuntu-latest-shard*
          path: shard-manifest/
          merge-multiple: true
      # HIMMEL-3897: green shards are not enough once a PR's shards run only
      # the impacted suites. Recompute the selection here (same base-sourced
      # script, same base, same merge commit) and require every ubuntu shard's
      # manifest to carry it verbatim, and the shards together to have run each
      # selected suite exactly once and green. A missing manifest, one from
      # another sha, or a shard that ran less than selected is red. The
      # aggregator's own `--list .` is the discovery a shard's `notfound` is
      # checked against: a suite it lists to RUN that no shard ran is red, so a
      # shard cannot drop one by filtering it or claiming notfound. Its tier and
      # changed-since filters MUST match the shards' env above (the impacted
      # filter stays off: the selection is checked separately).
      - name: Every shard ran exactly the selection
        env:
          IMPACTED_BASE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.base.ref == github.event.repository.default_branch && github.event.pull_request.base.sha || '' }}
          SUITE_TIER_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'pr' || 'all' }}
          SUITE_CHANGED_SINCE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.base.sha || '' }}
          # HIMMEL-5649: shards the plan left out because they had no suite. Empty
          # off a pull_request (every shard runs), where the plan job is skipped.
          ABSENT_SHARDS: ${{ needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.absent_shards || '' }}
          # HIMMEL-5556: the N the shards ran as, the same expression as their run step.
          SHARD_TOTAL: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.shard_total || 8 }}
        run: |
          bash scripts/ci/impacted-selection.sh "$IMPACTED_BASE" HEAD > shard-selection.txt
          head -n 2 shard-selection.txt
          bash scripts/ci/run-shell-tests.sh --list . > shard-discovered.txt
          bash scripts/ci/shard-manifest-verify.sh --dir shard-manifest --shards "$SHARD_TOTAL" --selection shard-selection.txt --discovered shard-discovered.txt --absent-ok "$ABSENT_SHARDS"
      # HIMMEL-3897 / HIMMEL-3896: the post-merge full sweep is where a
      # selector miss shows up — a suite red on main that the merged PR's
      # impacted selection did not list. Recorded, never blocking: the red
      # shards already fail this job; this names which reds a PR run would
      # have missed, for the selector's miss ledger.
      # HIMMEL-5113: main has no per-merge run, so a cron / dispatch run names
      # the merges it covers: the sha of the previous completed non-PR run on
      # main (any conclusion) up to this sha. Best effort -- an API failure or
      # no earlier run leaves `range` empty and never fails the job.
      - name: Merge range since the previous main run
        id: range
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          prev="$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?branch=main&status=completed&per_page=30" \
            --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.event != \"pull_request\" and .id < ${{ github.run_id }} and (.conclusion == \"success\" or .conclusion == \"failure\"))] | .[0].head_sha // empty" 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if [ -z "$prev" ]; then
            echo "no earlier completed main run found; merge range unknown" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "range=$prev..${{ github.sha }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          { echo "### Merges covered by this run ($prev..${{ github.sha }})"; echo '```'; git log --oneline "$prev..${{ github.sha }}" 2>&1 | head -n 100; echo '```'; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - name: Selector-miss ledger (main cron, red sweep)
        if: failure() && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && steps.range.outputs.range != ''
        env:
          RANGE: ${{ steps.range.outputs.range }}
        run: |
          awk '$1 == "ran" && $2 != "0" { print $3 }' shard-manifest/manifest-shard*.txt 2>/dev/null | sort -u > shard-red-suites.txt
          echo "red suites on this sweep: $(wc -l < shard-red-suites.txt)"
          rc=0
          bash scripts/cr/impacted-suites.sh --selector-miss "$RANGE" --red-file shard-red-suites.txt > selector-miss.txt || rc=$?
          { echo "### Selector-miss ledger ($RANGE, rc $rc)"; echo '```'; cat selector-miss.txt; echo '```'; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          cat selector-miss.txt
      - name: Upload selector-miss ledger
        if: failure() && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && steps.range.outputs.range != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: selector-miss-ledger
          path: |
            selector-miss.txt
            shard-red-suites.txt
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 90
      # Scoped to the schedule leg: that is the only leg where
      # SUITE_TIER_MODE=all actually exercises the extended tier (see
      # shell-unit-shard above), so only there does a red here plausibly mean
      # an extended suite broke rather than double-reporting a per-PR fast-
      # tier failure the PR gate already surfaced.
      - name: Extended-tier nightly issue — clear on green
        if: success() && github.event.schedule == '17 7 * * *'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: bash scripts/ci/shell-extended-nightly-issue.sh 0 "${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
      - name: Extended-tier nightly issue — file/refresh on red
        if: failure() && github.event.schedule == '17 7 * * *'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: bash scripts/ci/shell-extended-nightly-issue.sh 1 "${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"

  # HIMMEL-4912: the full guard-corpus replay (every row in a fresh bwrap
  # sandbox) takes ~143 min on a CI runner (1407s local x ~6; unmeasured here
  # until the first nightly), far past the 60-min shell-unit-shard cap, so it
  # runs in its own schedule-only job instead of a shard. PR CI and the
  # nightly shards run the fast subset (GUARD_CORPUS_TIER=fast). The 240-min
  # cap is the estimate x1.7; a red here is the nightly's own signal and
  # gates no PR.
  # ponytail: one job, serial; upgrade path: shard the replay (HIMMEL-5055).
  guard-corpus-full:
    if: github.event.schedule == '17 7 * * *'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Runs in the prebuilt CI image (docs/internals/ci-image.md). A fork or
    # dependabot[bot] run cannot pull the private package, so it gets '' (no
    # container) and the setup steps gated on !job.container.id install the
    # same tools on the host.
    # --init: an init as PID 1 reaps orphaned descendants, as on the host.
    # --privileged: bwrap and unshare need user namespaces inside the container.
    container:
      image: ${{ !(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository || github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]') && (vars.CI_IMAGE || 'ghcr.io/yotamleo-org/himmel-ci@sha256:6c7a604e4c615486e62303d70039361775a44b1ca3c04eb098a7b06cbbd85009') || '' }} # env-literal-ok: the CI image's own GHCR path, pinned by digest
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ github.token }}
      options: --init --user 1001 --privileged
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    timeout-minutes: 240
    # The image sets no locale (POSIX counts bytes); C.UTF-8 is the host runner's.
    env:
      LANG: C.UTF-8
      LC_ALL: C.UTF-8
    # A container's default run shell is sh; this is the host runner's default.
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash -e {0}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Record runner image (apt cache key)
        if: ${{ !job.container.id }}
        run: echo "APT_IMAGE=${ImageVersion:-unknown}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Cache apt debs (guard-corpus)
        if: ${{ !job.container.id }}
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/apt-archives
          key: apt-${{ runner.os }}-${{ env.APT_IMAGE }}-guard-corpus-${{ hashFiles('.github/scripts/apt-install.sh') }}
      - name: Install bubblewrap + socat
        if: ${{ !job.container.id }}
        run: bash .github/scripts/apt-install.sh bubblewrap socat
      - name: Allow unprivileged user namespaces (bwrap sandbox)
        run: sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0 || true
      - name: Full guard-corpus replay
        run: bash scripts/eval/guard-corpus/test-guard-corpus.sh
